What's new

The main changes in each version, newest first. Each chapter has the details.

0.2 (347)

  • Output starts off. Each time Kanau opens it sends nothing until you tap OUTPUT OFF at the top left and slide (chapter 02).
  • Kanau no longer sends over another sender on the same universe: it shows Blocked, with Join, Send … Only and Cancel. WAITING and Send anyway? are gone (chapter 02).
  • Output stops while Kanau is not on screen. SCREEN LOCK does not stop it (chapter 02).
  • LAMP MODE and Kanau Screen have six modes, four of them split into cells (chapters 02 and 03).
  • STAGE has no fade buttons any more; the six buttons are in each Scene's Settings → Fade (chapter 08).
  • A stored ★ color keeps the color temperature and G/M too (chapter 05).

0.2 (345)

  • A session is joined by QR code only. The guest scans the host's code, and works the light once the host taps Allow. Up to 8 guests can control at once (chapter 13).
  • Locks and limits belong to the console. No Scene records or applies them, so a recall never unlocks or re-limits a fixture (chapter 08).
  • Effects cross over with a Scene's fade instead of switching at the recall (chapter 08).
  • RENUMBER numbers every Scene 1, 2, 3 in list order, and a copy of 1 is named 1.1 (chapter 08).
  • COLOR works on what you select, down to single pixels, and opens for any selection (chapter 05).
  • GM sits at the right end of the status line. On iPhone, BLIND puts UPDATE in the place of BATTERY SAVE (chapter 01).

0.2 (341)

  • LAMP MODE turns an iPhone or iPad into a light that another console drives (chapter 02).
  • A Scene has a Delay and a Curve: S-CURVE, EASE IN or LINEAR. Each fixture's Delay counts from GO (chapter 08).
  • What you touch during a fade leaves it and is recorded into the Scene the fade is heading for (chapter 08).
  • A universe switched OFF is no longer sent at all (chapter 02).
  • The fluorescents are now FLUO FLICKER, FLUO DROPOUT, FLUO RESTART and FLUO DYING (chapter 09).
  • × closes a panel from the top left.

0.2 (329)

  • Grand Master Fade replaces Master Fade, and can be set in the GM panel as well (chapter 04).
  • ZEN: FINE sits under TILT, and the settings of each fader carry Remove fader (chapter 10).
  • Strap Lock works on iPad too, off by default there (chapter 10).

0.2 (327)

  • ZEN holds several faders: up to three on iPhone and five on iPad (chapter 10).
  • SIGNAL: NEXT STOPS AT chooses which signals NEXT stops for (chapter 09).
  • On iPad the Scenes have a row on Home, and large panels open in two columns (chapters 01 and 08).

QUICK START — try Kanau in 3 minutes

You do not need a single light to get this far. Button names are shown exactly as they appear on screen.

The app opens with a practice rig of 4 fixtures already patched. Three minutes here will show you most of how Kanau works.

1. Change the intensity

  1. Drag a fader up and down. The number above it and the color of the round icon change with it.
  2. Tap GM (GM 100 on iPad) at the top of the screen, and drag the grand master down in the panel that opens. The band at the top of the screen and its edge turn red.
  3. Tap →100 to bring it back, and close the panel.

A fader moves by the distance your finger travels, not the place you touched. Where you start makes no difference to the result.

2. Change the color

  1. Press and hold the round icon above a fader.
  2. The color panel opens. Intensity sets brightness, Color Temperature sets white, RGB sets color.
  3. The ‹ › at the top move you to the next fixture.

Every fixture carries different features, so the items you see change with it.

3. Recall a Scene

  1. Open the Scenes tab at the bottom.
  2. Four Scenes are waiting: DIM, COLOR, PIXELS, FX. Tap one.
  3. Back on Home, the faders and colors have changed to that look.

AUTO UPDATE is on to begin with, so anything you change after a recall is recorded back into that Scene. Switch the top of Scenes to MANUAL UPDATE, or lock the Scene, to leave it as it is (chapter 08).

See the values going out

Slide OUTPUT OFF at the top left to send (chapter 02). Then, even with no lights attached, Settings → DMX Monitor shows the numbers Kanau is actually sending. Move a fader and the numbers move with it.

What is in the practice rig

The demo has 4 fixtures from Generic: three RGBW and one BAR (4 pixels). They are in three groups, called KEY (two RGBW), BACK (one RGBW) and FLOOR (the BAR).

The grand master starts at 100, two fixtures (one RGBW and the BAR) are marked for BATTERY SAVE and carry a green label, FLOOR has a fire effect running, and four Scenes are saved. None of it claims to be a real product.

Connecting real lights

Once the demo makes sense, move to your own gear.

  1. Connect: put the iPhone on the same network as your DMX node. In Settings → Output, check that Nodes Answering is 1 or more. Then tap OUTPUT OFF at the top left of Home and slide to send; Network Output turns green (chapter 02). Gear that does not answer polling stays at 0 while receiving normally, so judge by the light itself in that case.
  2. Patch: Patch → ＋ New Patch → Add New Fixture, then set the model, DMX mode, universe and address. Match the fixture's own settings (chapter 03).
  3. Build the look: set intensity and color on Home (chapters 04 and 05).
  4. Save it: tap SAVE in Scenes to store the look (chapter 08).

The practice rig is an ordinary show. Delete it when you patch your own lights, or make a new one with Settings → Shows → New Show.

Five things worth knowing first

  1. Fixture Lock beats blackout. A locked fixture stays lit through B.O. (chapter 10).
  2. Under AUTO UPDATE a recalled Scene records what you do. Switch to MANUAL UPDATE, or lock it, to leave it alone (chapter 08).
  3. There are three kinds of lock. Fixture Lock holds the output, Scene Lock protects what a Scene has stored, Screen Lock stops stray touches (chapter 10). With Strap Lock on, the default, the screen also locks by itself when the iPhone hangs upside down. On iPad it is off until you turn it on. Lifting it does not unlock it; slide right, as with SCREEN LOCK.
  4. When the grand master is below 100, the band at the top of the screen turns red and its edge pulses red. If things look dim, look there first.
  5. Output starts off. Each time Kanau opens, tap OUTPUT OFF at the top left and slide to send. If another console is already sending on the same universe you will see Blocked, and SHARED if one appears later. Chapter 02 explains both.
WARNING

A fixture with Lock on will not go out when you press blackout, and will not go out when you pull the grand master to zero. Check that your locks are clear before a take. The count of what is still lit during a blackout is shown next to the green 🔒 at the top of the screen.

01 Reading the screen

What is on the Home screen, from the top down, and how to read it when something looks wrong.

Learn these seven first

Before the detailed tables, these are the only places you need to know.

PlaceWhat it does
GMOverall brightness, at the top of the screen
Fixtures / GroupsChooses which fixtures appear
FaderSets intensity
ScenesStores looks and brings them back
PatchRegisters fixtures
EffectsLists and stops running effects
SettingsOutput, shows, MIDI, session

Everything below is the detail.

The five tabs

Home is where you work. Tapping another tab opens a panel over it. Drag the handle at the top down, or tap × at the top left, to come back to Home. A panel opened from inside another one, such as DMX Monitor, has ‹ at the top left instead, and ‹ goes back one step. On iPad with iPadOS 18 or later the panels open almost to the size of the screen. COLOR, EFFECT, Patch and Scenes are laid out in two columns there when the window is wide enough.

TabWhat it is forSee
ScenesSaving and recalling looksChapter 08
PatchFixtures, addresses, modes, groupsChapter 03
HomeSetting intensity with fadersChapter 04
EffectsListing, adjusting and stopping effectsChapter 09
SettingsDMX output, shows, MIDI, session, LAMP MODE, preferencesChapters 02, 11–13

The status line

On the left is the send state. Each time Kanau opens it reads OUTPUT OFF, and nothing goes out until you tap it and slide (chapter 02). While sending it reads SENDING and the universes, such as SENDING U1 U2; where there is no room it becomes the route, a single letter: A for Art-Net, S for sACN, with a dot that pulses while DMX is going out. Bluetooth carries its own dot and name. Next to them is the name of the show you are in; on a narrow phone, where the row has no room to spare, it is left out. While BLIND is on, this whole left part becomes an amber BLIND; tap it to leave BLIND (chapter 08).

ShownMeaning
OUTPUT OFFNot sending since Kanau opened. Tap it and slide. With Slide to send under it, you moved something while output was off, and nothing went out
LISTENINGChecking for another sender before sending, for about a second
SENDING U1 U2Those universes are going out. A line such as U3 OFF means a patched universe that has not been slid open yet
Blocked U1Another sender is already on that universe, so Kanau does not send on it. Tap it for the choices (chapter 02)
Green dotSending
Amber dotSlowed down, or reconnecting (Reconnecting…)
Red dot, ART-NET No node or SACN No nodeNothing is answering. The status line names the route, shortened on a narrow screen. Tap it to open Settings → Output
Red dot, ART-NET Blocked or SACN BlockedSomething is stopping the output that will not clear by itself. The status line names the route and says Blocked, shortened on a narrow screen. Tap it to open Settings → Output, which prints the reason, and what to do about it, in red
Grey dot, IdleOutput is open but nothing is going out, for example with every universe switched off or no network on
SHARED and an IP or a device nameAnother console is sending to the same universe. This one is still sending too
JOINED or WATCH ONLY, and a nameIn a session. DMX goes out from the host

A green dot does not prove the light received anything. Chapter 02 explains how to check; chapter 14 covers what to do when it goes wrong.

The middle and right of the line carry these. GM sits at the right end, after SCREEN LOCK.

ItemTapHold, or note
GM 100Opens the grand master panelHold for its settings. On iPhone it reads GM, or just the number when it is down. Below 100 it is filled red and pulses
B.O.Clears the blackout. At GM 0 it opens the GM panel insteadReplaces GM while the console is dark. B.O. is also shown when GM is 0
U1 OFF (red)NothingWhich universes are switched off, by number. Up to three, then + for more. Turn them back on in Settings → Output
🔒 n (green)NothingWhat is still lit while the console is dark: locked fixtures, faders set as a switch that are ON, and locks left at an old address
BATTERY SAVETurns it on and offHold to set the amount and the fade. While it is on, it now and then shows the current amount, such as −50%. On iPhone, while BLIND is on, UPDATE takes its place and records the BLIND look into the current Scene (chapter 08)
UPDATE (iPhone)Records the current state into the recalled SceneIn the place of the show name while a Scene recalled under MANUAL UPDATE is current: blinking when there is something to record, dim when nothing differs. The send state takes its place when it has something to say
SCREEN LOCKDoes not lockHold for 0.5 seconds to lock the screen

U1 OFF and 🔒 appear only when there is something to report: the first when a patched universe is switched off, 🔒 while the console is claiming dark, which is a blackout or the grand master at zero. With Strap Lock on, hanging the iPhone upside down also locks the screen; slide right to unlock it.

The parts of Home

ItemHow to use it
Fixtures / GroupsSwitches between showing by model and showing by group. On iPad it sits in the status row at the top of Home
10 / 5Faders on a page. Five makes each one wider. On iPad it is 30 / 20 / 15 (40 / 20 on a 13-inch), in the status row
HISTORYOpens the list of earlier states. On iPad it sits in the status row, just right of the show name

CLEAR nClears the selection. The light does not change
‹ / ›Moves between pages
NumberIntensity from 0 to 100. Shown large at the top while you drag
Round fixture icon (…)Tap to select. Hold to open that fixture's panel
FaderDrag up and down to set intensity
Model nameMarks a run of the same model and mode
Number buttonThe fixture number. In piano mode it changes intensity while held

COLOR is unavailable with nothing selected; any selection opens it, even fixtures with no color (chapter 05). EFFECT needs a selection. PIXELS needs a pixel fixture on the page.

Colors and marks

Color or markMeaning
AmberSelected, or active
RedBlackout, a low grand master, a network problem, piano mode. Something to check
GreenSending. Fixture Lock. BATTERY SAVE on
Amber band and edgeBLIND is on. What you do does not reach the lights
PurpleOutput switched off, or the screen locked
CyanBeing worked by the other device in a session
OrangeAt a limit you set
GreyUnavailable, or stopped

The round icon carries the fixture's color and its real output. On a fixture with pixels it reads the cells as well, so one sitting at 100 with every cell down shows dark. A selection shows an amber rim, a switched-off output a purple ring and ⏻, a lock a green outer ring and 🔒. A color that gives no light, such as RGB all at 0, draws the circle as off even when the intensity is above 0. A running effect makes it move.

A red edge runs around the screen whenever the grand master is below 100, or during a blackout. The edge pulses, and a light travels around it. At zero — or in a blackout — the edge becomes thicker and deeper, and the light travels faster, so the two states are told apart without reading anything. A green edge, with a long light sliding slowly around it, means BATTERY SAVE is on. When both apply, the edge takes turns: red for about six seconds, green for about three. BLIND looks different: the band at the top of the screen, where the clock is, and the edge become one amber frame. If the grand master is down during BLIND, a red edge pulses on the amber frame. Green is not shown during BLIND. The edge says the output is being held down; the chip in the status line says by what.

02 Sending DMX — Output

Setting up the link to your lighting gear, and checking that it is getting there.

First connection

One Art-Net node

  1. Put the iPhone on the same Wi-Fi or wired network as the node.
  2. Open Settings → Output.
  3. Choose Art-Net and AUTO. Both are the defaults.
  4. Check that Nodes Answering is 1 or more. Some gear never answers polling and stays at 0 while it is receiving normally, so do not stop here if the figure will not move.
  5. On Home, tap OUTPUT OFF at the top left. A band opens under the status line; slide Slide to send to the right.
  6. The status line reads LISTENING for about a second, then SENDING U1, and Network Output turns green. Move a fader and watch the light respond.

Kanau never starts sending by itself. Each time it opens, output is off and the status line reads OUTPUT OFF; the patch, the destination and the switched-off universes are kept. Tap it and slide to send. Kanau first listens for about a second, and if no other sender is on a universe, it then sends every patched universe that is switched on, continuously, normally at 44 Hz. Changing between Art-Net and sACN, a network that was not there when you slid, leaving a session as a guest and leaving LAMP MODE put network output back to off, so slide again. A universe added to the patch later stays off until you slide, and the status line shows it as U3 OFF. Bluetooth connects when you slide, not at launch. Moving a fader or recalling a Scene never starts output; touch something while output is off and the status line shows Slide to send. Output stops while Kanau is not on screen and starts again when you come back; SCREEN LOCK does not stop it.

Settings in detail

Protocol and networks

Art-Net and sACN are exclusive: pick one. CRMX over Bluetooth runs alongside either.

Network lists your Wi-Fi, Ethernet and Hotspot connections with their addresses and how many nodes answered on each.

  • By default it uses every network available.
  • From the all-selected state, tapping one leaves only that one on. After that each tap turns one on or off.
  • With only one network, tapping it stops network output, and tapping it again goes back to using it.
  • Turn them all off and nothing goes out over the network. Bluetooth keeps sending.
  • A connection marked No address cannot be selected.

If you use wired and Wi-Fi together, check that both appear in the list.

Choosing the destination

SettingWhere it sendsWhen to use it
AUTO (Art-Net)Each universe by unicast to the nodes that list it in their reply; a node that lists none gets them all. A universe no node lists is broadcast every frame, unless an address is ticked in the list below. Broadcast only, if nothing answered and the list is emptyThe normal choice
BROADCAST (Art-Net)Every frame to each network's subnetWhen a node reports a wrong address and AUTO updates slowly
UNICASTStraight to the addresses you enterWhen broadcast does not reach, or you want to name the target
255.255.255.255 (Art-Net)Broadcast on the segment. Does not cross a routerWhen addressing does not line up and ordinary broadcast fails. iOS may block it
MULTICAST (sACN)The multicast address for each universeThe sACN default

With UNICAST, type the node's address and tap Add. The same list is shown under AUTO, for gear that does not answer polling. Every universe goes to every ticked address. Untick the box at the left of an address to stop sending to it while keeping it in the list; × removes it. With UNICAST and nothing ticked, a red line says No node IP is switched on or entered. No DMX is going out over the network.

If Nodes Answering is 1 or more on AUTO but a light does not respond, check whether the node is reporting the wrong address for itself. Look at Destination and try BROADCAST. Chapter 14 covers the other causes of lag.

RESCAN

Tapping RESCAN under Art-Net refreshes the node list. Use it after adding gear, removing gear or changing an address. Left alone, a new node appears within about 3 seconds and a removed one disappears after about 10.

Sending continues while it scans. RESCAN also measures the round trip to each node that answers. RESCAN is unavailable with no usable network.

When the output stops

In Settings → Output, a red line says what stopped the output and what to do about it: turn on the local network permission, switch to UNICAST and type the node's address, check the address you typed, check the Wi-Fi, give the node power. CRMX carries a line of its own. The console's own wording stays in brackets at the end, so it can be quoted exactly.

Universes and Art-Net numbering

Universes lists each patched universe with its fixture count, how many are lit, and an ON/OFF switch. A universe that is OFF reads Not sending, and so does one that has not been slid open yet.

IMPORTANT

OFF stops sending that universe. Nothing goes out for it on Art-Net or sACN, and over Bluetooth the link stays up but nothing is written. A receiver may keep its last values, so a light can stay lit. Which universes are switched off is named at the top of the screen, as U1 OFF.

If your node wants Net / Sub-Net / Universe instead of a single number, turn on Settings → Output → Art-Net → Net / Sub / Uni. The relationship is Net × 256 + Sub × 16 + Uni.

sACN priority can be 0, 100 or 200. It is 100 by default, and it is the priority Kanau sends with its sACN output.

CRMX over Bluetooth

  1. Turn on Bluetooth in Settings → Output → CRMX (Bluetooth).
  2. Allow Bluetooth the first time iOS asks.
  3. Pick a transmitter from the list. Tapping it again disconnects.

The transmitter you pick carries the universe your patch uses (U1 when the patch sits in universe 1). When the patch spans more than one universe, choose which one it carries with − and + on the Universe row under the transmitter; once you choose by hand, Kanau stops choosing for you until you disconnect the transmitter and pick it again. Next time, turning Bluetooth on reconnects to the same one, once you have slid to send. Scanning stops once the ones you picked are connected, so RESCAN is how you look for another transmitter. The list says connected for one that is linked and sending for one that data is going to. When a transmitter cannot connect or drops out, Settings → Output says what to check, with the system's own message in brackets.

With the same universe going out over both the network and Bluetooth, Settings → Output says so: U1: network and Bluetooth output are both on. That is a statement of fact, not a warning. A CRMX receiver takes the output of the transmitter it is linked to, so the same U1 on Kanau does not by itself feed one fixture twice. Flicker only happens where a fixture really is receiving from both paths; stop one of them there.

If a transmitter still refuses Art-Net after you turn Bluetooth off, check the transmitter's own settings.

When another console is found

ShownWhat it means, and what to do
Blocked U1When you slid, another sender was already on U1, so Kanau does not send on it. Tap it: the band names it, such as U1 In Use and the sender, and offers Join when it is a Kanau host, Send U2 Only when other universes are free, and Cancel. There is no way to send over it
SHARED + IP or a device nameAnother console appeared after this one started. Sending continues, so stop one of them if you need to

Kanau devices tell each other which universes they send, so two that slide at once do not both send. sACN, unicast senders and Bluetooth in other apps may not be visible from here.

LAMP MODE — this device as a light

LAMP MODE turns this iPhone or iPad into a light that another console drives over Art-Net or sACN. Open Settings → LAMP MODE, the last heading. Choose Art-Net or sACN, choose a MODE from the list — RGB 6ch, HUE SAT 5ch, RGB 2 CELLS 9ch, RGB 4 CELLS 15ch, HUE SAT 2 CELLS 9ch or HUE SAT 4 CELLS 15ch — and set Universe and Address, by typing them or with − and +. The line under them shows which addresses each part takes. Tap START. It is not offered while BLIND is on.

The screen turns the color it receives and reads WAITING until the first data arrives; if the data stops, it keeps the last color. Each mode starts with Screen Dimmer and ends with Back Light and Vibration. Between them, RGB 6ch has Red, Green and Blue and HUE SAT 5ch has Hue and Saturation; the CELLS modes split the screen into 2 halves or 4 quarters, each with its own Red, Green and Blue, or its own Dimmer, Hue and Saturation, numbered from the top left. Hue 0 to 255 covers the whole circle. Screen Dimmer dims the screen only. Back Light is the light on the back of the device and Vibration its vibration; a device without one leaves it out. On the other console, patch it as Kanau Screen (chapter 03). On Art-Net it answers polling as Kanau Screen, so it shows by that name in the other console's list of nodes.

To leave, slide the switch at the top right across, then tap the × that appears. While LAMP MODE is on, this device sends no DMX, MIDI is off, the screen is at full brightness and does not lock itself, and a guest leaves its session. Leaving puts the brightness and MIDI back, with output off again.

DMX Diagnostics — reading what is happening

The lower half of Output is there to show you where things stopped. It is not a set of settings. When output is slow or missing, read it from the top (chapter 14).

ItemHow to read it
DestinationWhere it is really going. ↦ after an address means unicast to a node that answered
MediumThe connections in use, for example Wi-Fi + Ethernet
Network OutputPackets sent over the network in the last second. Around 44 is normal. Nothing means none went out, as before you slide. Bluetooth is not counted here
ClockThe worst gap between sends. About 23 ms is normal. Over 100 ms points at the phone
Touch → DMXFrom your finger to the packet. About 25 ms is normal
Nodes AnsweringHow many answered, with name, address, connection and round trip. The round trip is blank until RESCAN measures it; the figure in brackets is the worst of the last 10 seconds. On AUTO, the line under each node lists the universes sent to it, such as U1 or U0–U3
Type these into the nodeThe Net / Sub / Uni to enter on the node, when that display is on

These narrow the problem down; they do not prove success. They are what Kanau sent, and whether the light received it cannot be seen from here. Network Output can be green while a mismatch or a fault at the other end keeps the lights dark. Gear that does not answer polling shows 0 under Nodes Answering even while it is receiving.

DMX Monitor

Settings → DMX Monitor shows all 512 channels of each universe as they go out. It refreshes 10 times a second. Reading it does not affect sending. A universe that is not going out, because it is OFF or has not been slid open, shows its heading with OFF and no values.

The cells only show values; nothing can be typed here. A lock whose fixture has been deleted is listed above the grid, with UNLOCK.

The values read as percent or as raw DMX, following the same setting as the rest of the console. Each universe folds away on its own; a folded heading keeps the count of channels still showing, so you can see which one is busy without opening it.

03 Patching fixtures — Patch

Register the lights you are using, and set the model, DMX mode, universe, address, number and groups.

Intensity and color are set on Home (chapters 04 and 05).

Adding fixtures

  1. Open Patch → ＋ New Patch and tap Add New Fixture to show the fields.
  2. Choose Manufacturer → Fixture → Mode. The mode must match the one set on the fixture itself. Each of the three opens as a list of its own with a search field, so a long list of models is a matter of typing rather than scrolling.
  3. Set how many, the universe and the start address.
  4. Check the range and any warnings, then tap Add. It is saved as it is added.
FieldWhat it is
FavoritesA ★ sits beside each mode, the Mode field and each manufacturer; tap it to add or remove. Starred modes appear as buttons under Favorites, starred manufacturers go to the top of the list, and Edit beside Favorites lists them all
NameThis fixture's own name. It appears in Patch and the Patch List; Home shows the Label instead. Defaults to the model name
Number / How ManyThe number you call it on the floor, and how many to add, up to 4,096. The number may be left empty; it starts at the highest in use plus one
LabelThe display name shared by every fixture of that model in the same mode. It runs under the faders. Defaults to the official model name; change Mode here and a Label you have not typed follows the new mode. It can also be typed in the fixture's panel (chapter 06)
Universe / AddressDefaults to U1 / 1. Changing the universe resets the address to 1. U0 is allowed
OffsetThe spacing between fixtures. Filled in from the mode's channel count
GapExtra channels to leave between fixtures
BATTERY SAVEMarks the new fixtures for BATTERY SAVE
Label ColorThe background of the number. Seven colors, or none
MapThe 512-channel layout. Drag and release to set the start address

Each fixture after the first starts at the previous start address plus Offset and Gap, but never closer than the mode's channel count, so the addresses do not overlap. Anything past 512 goes into the next universe. An Offset smaller than the mode's channel count raises a warning, but you can carry on.

Afterwards a panel lists what went in — one row per fixture, with its number, name and address — under a line like Added 3 × Titan Tube — U1 1–15. It stays until you tap OK, so you can keep patching and read it after. Patched, under the form, lists the models already patched; tap a row to open the form with that model and mode filled in.

Two kinds of number

NumberWhat it is
Unit No.A running number within the model. Assigned for you
Fixture NumberThe number you use on the floor. You set it

Which one Home shows is set in Settings → Settings → Fixture Numbers → Show the Fixture Number. Unit No. is the default. Duplicate fixture numbers raise a warning but are allowed.

Models and modes

This version ships with 61 manufacturers, 1,081 fixtures and 15,477 modes. For anything not in the library, use the Generic definitions or Custom Fixtures.

Generic includes Dimmer, Dimmer 16-bit, Bi-color, CCT, RGB, RGBW, Dimmer + RGB and Dimmer + RGBW. Bulb and Desk lamp are listed under the manufacturer Tungsten. Kanau Screen, under the manufacturer Kanau, is a device in LAMP MODE (chapter 02): one Add patches three fixtures in a row — Kanau Screen, Kanau Back Light and Kanau Vibration — in any of the six modes of LAMP MODE (chapter 02). The number in a mode's name is the channels the three take together, and the CELLS modes split the screen into pixels, opened with PIXELS.

  • PROVISIONAL (Advanced): a placeholder mode, used where the DMX chart has not been worked through. It sends intensity on channel 1 and nothing else.
  • Modes with no dimmer channel: the fader drives the color channels together, acting as a virtual dimmer.

Changing patched fixtures

Patched lists fixtures by model and mode. Inside a model, and in the All row, the fixtures follow the order of the faders on Home (chapter 04). Tap a heading to fold it. Tap a fixture's row to open its patch settings.

Patch List, under the Patched heading, shows every patched fixture in address order, universe by universe. Each row reads the universe and the start address large with the end address under it, the fixture's number, then its name and mode; modes are never cut short. It is there to read while you set addresses on the fixtures themselves; nothing in it can be changed. An overlapping start address is red and marked ⚠. Export PDF at the top right makes an A4 copy to hand out, with the show name and the date on each page. Fader Order, which opens the order of the faders on Home, is not in this row; it is inside the All row, each group and each model once you open them (chapter 04).

Fixture Sheet, in Settings just below DMX Monitor, shows how every fixture is right now, in the order of All on Home: number and name, address, intensity, color, any running effect, and marks such as LOCK and OFF. Nothing in it can be changed, and Export PDF makes a copy. With groups in the patch, ALL and a button for each group under the title narrow the list without changing Home, and Export PDF then asks whether to take that group or everything.

Labels, in Settings below Fixture Sheet, makes stickers for the fixtures as an A4 PDF, in address order. Standard is 52.5 × 37.125 mm, 32 to a sheet; Small is 26.25 × 14.85 mm, 160 to a sheet. Copies sets 1 to 4 per fixture. Each label carries the fixture number, the Label, the start address and the mode. Under the preview, Page 1 of 3 says how many sheets there are, and ‹ › step through them. Export PDF saves it.

⚠ marks an overlapping address or a run past channel 512. It also marks a fixture whose output is being held at other values, by a lock; open the fixture to see it. Sending continues while it is showing, so check the settings. n fixture data problems refers to faults found while loading fixture data; tap it for the detail.

Working in this list does not change which fixtures Home is showing.

Changing many at once

Tap Select Many and choose the fixtures. The ✓ on a model row takes all of that model. Each ✓ shows the order you picked it in, from 1, and naming, numbering and addressing follow that order. A fixture is ticked only in the row you tapped, not in its other rows.

ActionWhat it does
Select All / Select NoneTakes or clears everything, folded rows included
NameNumbers the end of the name in the order you selected
NumberSets fixture numbers in the order you selected
AddressRe-lays them from a universe, start address and gap
BatteryMarks or unmarks them for BATTERY SAVE
New groupBuilds a group from the selection
DeleteRemoves them. Check the count before you confirm

Deleting a fixture also removes its intensity, color and limits, and takes it out of every Scene. HISTORY can undo it. Deleting from within a group only removes it from that group; the fixture itself stays. If that leaves the group empty, the group is deleted too, and the confirmation says so.

Re-patch — moving into free space

  1. Open Patch → Re-patch.
  2. In the address-ordered list, choose the fixture to move.
  3. Tap a free range. It moves to the start of it.

Only ranges large enough are offered. Overlapping fixtures are shown in red.

Close Gaps, at the top right of Re-patch, packs the fixtures of one universe from address 1, in address order. Gaps you left on purpose are closed up too. It lists only the fixtures that move, with Before and After, and nothing changes until you tap Apply. The fixtures' own DMX addresses do not change: set each fixture to its After value. Locked addresses keep their previous values. The whole pack is one step in HISTORY.

Building groups

  1. Tap ＋ New Group and give it a name.
  2. Choose the fixtures in the order you want them on Home.
  3. Tap CREATE.

A fixture can be in several groups. It is not copied: changing it from any group changes the same fixture. Adding it to a group leaves it in All.

Tapping a group name lets you set the name, see the count and address range and layout, or delete it. Edit Group adds fixtures to the group; Add to an Existing Group puts the current selection into a group you already have.

Group Order, in the row under ＋ New Group, sets the order of the groups. It appears once there are two or more groups, and is not shown to a guest. Drag the handle at the right of a row; Home's model and group buttons and this list then follow the same order. All is not in the list and always comes first. Each move is one step in HISTORY.

Whether Patch shows an All row is set in Settings → Settings → Groups → Show the All Row.

Fixtures not in the library (Advanced)

Custom Fixtures holds definitions you add yourself. It is on the Patch tab, under ＋ New Patch and the list of models. They are available to every show. Deleting a definition does not affect fixtures already patched from it.

From GDTF Share

  1. Open ＋ Browse GDTF Share and SIGN IN with your GDTF Share account.
  2. REFRESH the list, then choose manufacturer, fixture, revision and mode. Search covers every manufacturer.
  3. Read the import report and choose SAVE, SAVE & EDIT or SAVE & PATCH.

SAVE & PATCH opens the patch screen with that definition selected. Remember on This Device stores your sign-in; FORGET removes it. Definitions you already fetched stay. Your sign-in goes to GDTF Share.

From a GDTF file

＋ Import a GDTF File, then ＋ Import a GDTF File again in the panel that opens, pick the .gdtf, check the mode and the import report, then save. No network is needed.

The report lists what could not be carried over. A 16-bit value split across distant addresses keeps only its coarse byte, unused addresses are held as empty slots, and channels on another DMX break are dropped. Where addresses overlap, the earlier channel wins. Unknown functions keep their original names.

A definition marked Imported data is not verified. should be checked against the real fixture. Fix wrong roles with SAVE & EDIT; the fix applies to fixtures you patch from it afterwards. This mode has no channels. means you should pick a different mode.

By hand, from a DMX chart

Open ＋ Build by Hand and start from Build It Yourself, an empty definition, or a template: Intensity, CCT, Bi-color, RGB, HSI, x, y, CCT + HSI, Intensity + RGBW, Full Color, Full Color + White, Multi-emitter or Pixel. The second choice, Copy an Existing Fixture, starts from a fixture in the library instead (below).

Give each channel a label, and set the role, 8 or 16 bit, default and real-world unit as needed. Channel numbers and the total are worked out for you. Leave a slot unused if you do not know its role, and you can still drive it from Channels. Save is refused while there is an ERROR. Each channel also has a Pixel: None, or a number. Channels with the same number make one pixel, marked P1, P2 and so on in the table. When several Intensity channels have no Pixel, an amber note says they move together on one fader; give each its own Pixel to control them separately. The Pixel template asks for Each Pixel, the template one pixel is built from, and Pixels, how many, and repeats the channels that many times.

By copying an existing one

Open ＋ Build by Hand → Copy an Existing Fixture and choose Manufacturer, Fixture and Mode. The copy is named "… (Modified)" and is listed under MODIFIED in the Manufacturer list. Duplicate and Edit lets you change the name, the color temperature range (shown only when there is a CCT channel), channel roles and names, labels and defaults. The channel count, the 16-bit layout, the ranges and the switch structure cannot be changed.

04 Setting intensity — Home

The faders on Home. This is the heart of Kanau.

Moving a fader

A fader responds to the distance your finger travels, not to the place you touched. You can drive it from the number, the round icon, or the empty space below the fader. It is built so you can work while looking at the stage instead of your hand.

The knob grows a little as you touch it, and nothing moves until you have dragged a short way, so resting a finger on it is safe. The light along the fader goes out when the number above it reads 0, so a fader at 0 never looks like it is at 1. While you drag, the number, the name shown under the faders and the value appear large at the top of the screen. If you have set limits, it moves within them. A light tap comes the moment the fader you are moving reaches its upper or lower limit, including a limit you set; it is not repeated while you stay there. ZEN and the grand master do the same. A locked fixture, or a guest that cannot write, gets none. On a fixture that carries color, the readout also shows that color as a band, the color temperature in kelvin, G or M with a number when the green / magenta tint is off neutral, and the name of the gel you picked from a table, for as long as the color is still the one you set. A color that only happens to match a gel is not named; a white is named from its kelvin value. A plain dimmer shows none of that, and the grand master never shows a color, because it is not one fixture.

FINE

ActionWhat happens
Short tapCycles normal → FINE (1/10) → FINE+ (1/20) → normal
HoldThe next step while held. Back to normal when you let go

Switching mid-drag does not make the value jump. FINE also applies to raw channels and to Pan and Tilt.

Moving several at once

Select two or more round icons, then drag one of the faders. They all move by the same amount, keeping the differences between them. When one reaches a limit the others carry on. Locked fixtures are left out.

This is not the same as working several fixtures in the COLOR panel, where they all land on the same value. The exception there is the ratio row under Intensity, which scales each fixture from its own level (chapter 05).

The number buttons as a piano

The ＋ − button at the bottom right sets the mode.

ModeWhile a number button is held
LOCK (the default)Nothing changes
＋Goes to the Piano ＋ level, 100 by default. Never above the fixture's upper limit, and never lowers a fixture that is already higher
−Goes to the Piano − level, 0 by default. Never below the fixture's lower limit, and never raises a fixture that is already lower

Let go and it returns to where it was. You can hold several at once, or slide sideways to play them in turn. Locked fixtures do not respond.

The buttons turn red while ＋ or − is armed. It is always LOCK at launch. The two levels are set in Settings → Settings → PIANO → Piano ＋ and Piano −, for this device; when either differs from 100 or 0, the ＋ − button shows it, as ＋80 or −20.

⏻ — output only

Tapping ⏻ turns a fixture's output off and on while keeping the value. It turns purple while off, and the number stays. Moving the fader while it is off does not light anything. A tap fades over Power Fade — SNAP, 0.5, 1, 1.5 or 2 seconds, 1.5 by default — set in Settings → Settings → Fade Times.

ON/OFF is the default. In the fixture's Power Switch you can change it to FLASH ON or FLASH OFF, which last only while held, or to NONE. Locked fixtures do not respond.

The fifth choice is LOCK: the square then turns that fixture's lock on and off. A square set to LOCK is the one thing a lock does not stop — if it did, a locked fixture could never be unlocked from here.

A fader as a switch

Turn on Switch in a fixture's panel (chapter 06) and its fader becomes a rocker the full length of the fader: ON at the top, OFF at the bottom. Each tap switches it the moment you press. ON goes to the upper limit and OFF to the lower limit, and the number above reads ON or OFF. Dragging, FINE and ZEN do not work on it. When it is OFF, the lower face is a bright plate with OFF in bold and the upper face is flat. If B.O. or BATTERY SAVE is holding its output down, it looks OFF too: the number above reads OFF, the lower face is the plate with an edge of purple for B.O. or green for BATTERY SAVE, and the upper face is flat. When the hold ends it shows ON again, because its own ON or OFF was never changed.

GM and intensity effects do not lower it. If the fixture is marked for BATTERY SAVE, it turns OFF while BATTERY SAVE is on. It changes at once, with no fade, and its own ON or OFF is left as it was, so it returns when BATTERY SAVE is turned off or when you turn on Skip BATTERY SAVE for that fixture. B.O. turns it off, and ⏻ and Lock work as usual. A value that arrives another way, from a Scene, MIDI or the COLOR panel, lands on ON at 50 or above and on OFF below 50. In a Scene fade it switches at the start. With the piano, ＋ is ON and − is OFF while held.

GM and B.O.

Tapping GM at the top opens the grand master fader, B.O. and →100.

  • The GM fader sets overall brightness. It is relative, and FINE works on it.
  • B.O. turns the blackout on and off. The GM value is kept.
  • →100 appears when GM is below 100, and puts it back.

Holding GM opens a panel with 100, 75, 50, 25, 12.5 and B.O. B.O. there turns the blackout on; it does not set GM to zero. On iPad the panel has these down the left, the fader in the middle and the fade buttons down the right. On iPhone they are across the top, the fade buttons at the bottom, and the fader takes the room between.

The fade for these buttons is Grand Master Fade: SNAP, 0.5, 1, 1.5 or 2 seconds, in the panel you get by holding GM and in Settings → Settings → Fade Times. Both set the same value. SNAP is the default. The fade starts gently, is fastest in the middle and lands gently; the time is the whole fade. A guest in a session does not see it. Dragging the fader with a finger is always immediate.

WARNING

A fixture with Lock on does not respond to GM or B.O. It stays lit. The count of what is still lit during a blackout, locked fixtures included, is shown next to the green 🔒 at the top of the screen.

Choosing what is on the page

Fixtures shows by model and mode; Groups shows All and the groups you built. Tap a name to switch. One fader is always one fixture, even inside a group.

The order under All starts grouped by model, then in patch order, and a group starts in the order you built it. You can change any of them (see Changing the order of the faders below).

‹ and › change page. On the last page, › goes to the first page of the next model (the next group, under Groups); on the first page, ‹ goes to the last page of the previous model. They stop at the very ends, and never go into or out of All. Swiping across the band with ‹ and › does the same. Switching between 10 and 5 keeps the fixture you are working on in view. While you hold a fader, none of these — the names, ‹ and ›, 10 and 5, PIXELS or PIANO — changes what is on the page; pressing one gives a warning vibration instead.

Changing the order of the faders

The faders on Home go in an order you can change. Each page keeps its own: All, every group and every model. Only the order of the columns changes. The light, the limits, the locks, the fixture number and the unit number stay with the fixture.

There are two ways in. The first is Fader Order in Patch. Open the All row, a group or a model under Patched and it is inside: in a group it sits between Edit Group and Delete Group, and in All it is the only one. It is not shown to a guest, and Patch is closed while BLIND is on. It opens a list of the faders in order, starting from the page you pressed it in, with ‹ at the top left. A menu at the top chooses All, a group or a model, and Reset Order beside it rebuilds the page the list is showing, from the same bases as RESET ORDER below. Each row shows the fader's place at the left, then the fixture's number in thin type, and its name as it is in Patch (the model's name when none is set), on its Label Color when it has one, and a handle at the right. Hold the handle and drag the row up or down: the rows around it move aside, and it goes in where you let go. One row moves at a time. An amber line under a row marks the end of a page of Home, every 10 or 5 faders. When a fixture on the page has PIXELS open, the list numbers fixtures rather than faders, and no amber lines are shown.

The second way is to make Home itself the editor. Hold the heading above the faders, the one with the page name and ‹ ›. The heading turns into ‹ REORDER, the page name, [n/m] › and DONE, and the faders are dimmed and do not respond, so touching them changes no brightness. Hold a column, from the icon down to the fader, and drag it sideways: the column keeps its look, with a thin green edge, and follows your finger, and the columns in between slide over by one place to open the spot where it will go in. It settles there when you let go. While you hold it, its round icon turns green and shows a number: the place it will take if you let go now, counted through all the pages of that chip (All, a group or a model), one number per fixture, the same as in the Fader Order list. The lifted column stays within the columns and never reaches the buttons along the bottom. A column can cross pages: drag it until its outer edge is over the last column of the page (or the first), and hold it there for about half a second, and the page turns. While you wait, the › (or ‹) in the heading fills with a green ring; if you move back or let go before it fills, the page does not turn and the column goes in where it is. Grabbing a column does not start the wait; it starts once the column has moved. Staying there turns no more pages; take the column off the edge and back to turn the next one. It never turns past the first or last page, and the page-name chips such as All or a group do not change. It goes in on the page showing when you let go. ‹ and ›, and the buttons that choose the page, still work, and carry on reordering the page you pressed. A fixture with PIXELS open moves as one block. It will not start while a finger is on a fader, and a warning vibration says so. In place of the buttons along the bottom there is one key, RESET ORDER. Press it and choose a base: Patch Order, Fixture Number, DMX or Model (a model's page has no Model). The page being reordered is rebuilt the moment you choose, as one step in HISTORY; pressing the key alone, or Cancel, changes nothing. Tap DONE to finish. It also ends when you leave Home, when the app goes to the background, when you become a guest, and when you enter or leave BLIND. GM, BATTERY SAVE and SCREEN LOCK keep working during it.

The order belongs to the show: it is saved in the show file, and a guest sees the same order. Only the host, or a device on its own, can change it. One move is one step in HISTORY, shown as order. MIDI knobs and number keys follow positions, so they follow the new order; so do the direction of an effect, the direction of PIXELS and the rows of the Fixture Sheet.

A show with no order of its own opens in Model order; on a device that had been set to By fixture number before this version, it opens in Fixture Number order the first time. Fixture Number in Reset Order sorts once, when you choose it; typing the fixture numbers again later does not re-sort the faders.

The buttons along the bottom

COLOR needs a selection. EFFECT takes one too, but it also opens with nothing selected while something is running anywhere on the rig; it goes grey only when nothing is selected and nothing is running. PIXELS goes grey when it has nothing to open: with a selection, when no selected fixture on the page has pixels; with none, when no fixture on the page has pixels.

Working pixels on their own

Tapping PIXELS opens the cells of the selected pixel fixtures on the page, or of every pixel fixture on the page when nothing is selected, as their own faders; it never opens or closes a fixture on another page. They follow the fixture's own fader with the keys .1, .2 and so on, and each carries its own intensity and color. Tap again to fold them. Folding a fixture lets go of its pixel selection.

A fixture with pixels carries P above its value. A fixture whose pixel order is inverted (chapter 06) carries R instead, and its pixel faders run the other way: the leftmost is the last pixel.

Selecting a cell opens PIXELS for its fixture. A fixture is selected whole or by cell, never both: a fixture selected whole shows a faint ring on its cells, and tapping one cell lets go of just that cell. Select more than one cell and they move together on one fader, the same way fixtures do: each keeps its distance from the others, and the ones that reach an end stop there.

CLEAR n only clears the selection. Values and outputs are untouched.

05 Setting color — COLOR

Color and intensity for one fixture or many.

NOTE

What you see depends on what the fixture actually has. A one-channel dimmer shows only Intensity. Kanau does not show controls a fixture does not have.

Opening the panel

HowWhat it works on
Hold a fixture iconThat one fixture
Hold a cell iconThat cell
Select round icons, then COLOR, or hold one of the selected iconsEverything selected. A fixture with PIXELS closed counts whole; with PIXELS open, its pixels count — all of them when its own icon is selected, or only the pixel icons you selected
Hold a model or group buttonEvery fixture in it. All means every fixture

‹ and › appear in the panel opened from a fixture in the Patch tab, and in the panel opened by holding one fixture's round icon on Home. They move to the previous or next fixture of the current Home scope (All, a model or a group), across pages, and stop at the ends. The DIM / COLOR or MOVE choice is kept, and a Label, Name or number you have typed is committed before the move. They do not appear on a cell's panel or on a panel for several fixtures. A panel for a selection names what it works on under its title, such as 3 pixels or 2 fixtures; color, Intensity and the limits then act on those alone, and pixels you did not select stay as they are. Any selection opens COLOR, even fixtures with no color: the panel then has Intensity, the limits, Lock and the other settings but no color, and in a mix only the fixtures that have color take it.

On iPhone a line at the bottom of the panel names the Scene you are working in: a red A with RECORDING under AUTO UPDATE, an amber M with UPDATE under MANUAL UPDATE, and LOCKED in green for a locked Scene. UPDATE there records the current state into that Scene, as UPDATE in Scenes does; it can be pressed when it blinks.

Intensity and color

ItemHow it works
Intensity0 to 100, by slider, typing, ± buttons, presets or the ratio keys
Color Temperature (CCT)In kelvin, within the fixture's range
Green / MagentaThe green–magenta correction. The 0 button returns it to neutral
CrossfadeThe balance between the white side and the color side. Which way round is up to the fixture
RGB and emittersR, G, B, W, Amber, Lime, Cyan and whatever else the fixture carries
Hue / Saturation / CIE x / CIE yShown on fixtures that have them

Intensity ±5 and ±10 snap to multiples of 5 or 10: from 47, +10 gives 50. With several fixtures selected, each one moves from its own level: a fixture at 100 stays at 100 on +, one at 0 stays at 0 on −, and a locked fixture does not move. The presets are 0, 10, 20, 30, 50, 75 and 100. When the selected fixtures are at different levels, the number reads — in amber, no preset lights, and the slider stays at the first fixture's level; it goes back to a number once they match. Below a dividing line, 1/8, 1/4 and 1/2 set the level to that part of what it is now, and ×2, ×4 and ×8 multiply it, up to 100. With two or more fixtures or pixels that have intensity, the Intensity section of the GRADIENT tab (below) has one field. It starts empty and shows the levels as you press the keys, such as 0 THRU 100 THRU 0, with that same row written under it as an example. Tap it and a keypad opens below (7 8 9 THRU, 4 5 6 DEL, 1 2 3 C, 0 ENTER; the phone's keyboard is not used); tap the field again to close it without changing anything. Type levels with THRU between them and press ENTER, which sets the fixtures and closes the keypad. If the first key you press is a digit, a new row of levels starts; THRU or DEL carries on from the old row, and ENTER sets it again. With two levels, the fixtures go in even steps from the first to the second, in fader order. 0 THRU 100 THRU 0 goes up and back, so the middle lands on 100: with five fixtures, 0, 50, 100, 50, 0. Otherwise each level sits on the nearest fixture and the ones between follow a straight line, and a level that falls exactly between two fixtures gives both the same value: with ten fixtures, 0 → 100 → 0 → 50 → 10 gives 0, 50, 100, 50, 0, 0, 25, 50, 30, 10. One level sets every fixture to it. A locked fixture does not move, each fixture stays inside its own limits, and it works with mixed models. Each ENTER is one step in HISTORY.

The CCT presets are 2700, 3000, 3200, 4300, 5000, 5600, 6500 and 10000 K. Beyond the fixture's range you land on its limit, marked MIN or MAX. A fixture with only two color temperatures shows two buttons instead of a slider.

Where a fixture has more than one crossfade, the later ones appear just above the controls they feed.

Gels

ItemWhat it is
Gel presetsLEE and Rosco presets for fixtures with RGB. Separate tables for 3200 K and 5600 K
Preset / GelThe fixture's own built-in gels or color presets, chosen by number
Gels → x/yThe makers' own CIE x/y tables, for fixtures with x and y: LEE, 295 filters, and Rosco, 1,079. Choose the light source from the menu at the top. Once you pick one, the key reads that gel, such as LEE 002 Rose Pink, until x or y is changed another way. Rows sit under the maker's own headings, and Rosco's discontinued filters carry its mark. Roscolene is not included

The RGB values under Gel presets come from Astera's published color data. They carry no brightness, so set that with the fader. With a fixture's built-in presets, the app cannot always show which one is selected. The x/y tables are the makers' values, sent as they are; Rosco's are its myColor figures, which use the 10° observer. On a fixture whose Crossfade runs from a color temperature to a color, picking a color with the picker, a gel preset or Gels → x/y moves a Crossfade that sits at the color-temperature end over to the color end, so the color shows.

The list stays open after you pick, so you can try one after another. A long list has an index down its right edge — the hundreds of the gel number, or the first letter of each heading — and tapping one jumps there. Close it with ✕ at the top left. Whether it appears at all is set in Settings → Settings → Gels → Gel presets.

Saving colors you use often

  • Save this color stores a color under ★. It is kept per model and mode, and holds the Crossfade and, where the fixture has them, the color temperature and G/M. A ★ stored before this version has neither and leaves them as they are.
  • Save this temperature stores a color temperature. That one is shared across models.

Tap a stored button to apply it. Hold to rename, edit or delete.

Advanced Color

Advanced Color gathers the controls the app works out for itself, rather than the fixture's own channels.

In the picker, hue runs across and saturation down. Brightness is the fader's job. Tap anywhere to place the color. To drag it, take the round handle; a drag that starts anywhere else scrolls the panel.

RGB, the Hue and Saturation worked out from RGB, and CMY (255 − RGB) appear on fixtures that can take them. On a fixture that takes only Hue and Saturation, or only x and y, they restate the fixture's color at full strength, and setting them reaches the light; brightness stays with the fader. A fixture's own Hue, Saturation or CMY channels are not repeated here.

Several fixtures, and several models

In this panel, whatever you touch lands on the same value for everything selected. That is true of the color sliders, the Intensity presets from 0 to 100, typing and the stored colors alike. Intensity is the exception for moving: its slider, its ± buttons and the ratio row under it (1/8 to ×8) move each fixture from its own level, so their differences stay. The GRADIENT tab is the other exception: its color layout and its THRU row give each fixture something different on purpose. To move colors while keeping their differences, select the faders on Home instead.

With two or more fixtures selected, or two or more pixels with PIXELS open, a GRADIENT tab sits beside DIM / COLOR, as DIM / COLOR | MOVE | GRADIENT, or DIM / COLOR | GRADIENT when none of them has a MOVE panel. It is not there for one closed fixture, a single pixel, or the panel opened from Patch, and a panel last left on GRADIENT opens on DIM / COLOR in those cases. GRADIENT opens with an Intensity section, which holds the keypad field, and below it a Color section, with the layout buttons described under Coloring along the pixels below and a color band for whatever the layout is setting. The Color section appears only for fixtures of one model in one mode with PIXELS closed; with anything else, GRADIENT holds only Intensity. The DIM / COLOR tab itself has no layout buttons and no keypad row: it writes the same color to everything selected.

With different models selected, only Intensity, CCT, G/M and ★ appear. Open one model on its own to set RGB and emitters. CCT is held within each fixture's own range.

Pixels and repeated color groups

Hold a cell icon to set that cell's color and intensity. Changing the body color sets every cell; a cell you changed by hand keeps its own. The body Intensity applies across all the cells. Intensity on a cell's own panel moves that cell only.

Where a mode carries the same color role more than once, such as Gel 1 and Gel 2, the later groups appear lower in the panel. Every color group is stored in a Scene, and comes back with it as long as the fixture is still in the same mode.

Coloring along the pixels — PIXELS

With PIXELS open on Home, the COLOR panel of a pixel fixture starts with a PIXELS section. It lays color out along the pixels in one go, on every fixture you have selected. It appears only where the pixels carry color that Kanau can write. Select only some pixels and it works on just those, as one line in their order on Home, with no EACH or ACROSS.

ButtonWhat it lays out
SOLIDEvery pixel follows the fixture's own color, as before
GRADIENTSTART on the first pixel, END on the last, blended in between
ALTERNATECOLOR 1 and COLOR 2 taking turns, or three colors with COLOR 3
RAINBOWThe hue circle along the pixels

The button you pressed lights amber, and so does the end or color you are setting — START, END, or COLOR 1 to COLOR 3. The sliders, presets and gels below then write to that one. There is nothing to confirm: the light changes as you go, and HISTORY steps back.

  • GRADIENT: Spread narrows or widens the blend. The blend runs through color temperature too, so START can be a warm white and END a color, on pixels that have those channels
  • ALTERNATE: Colors sets two or three, and Pixels per Color how many pixels each one takes
  • RAINBOW: Start Hue is the hue of the first pixel, and Span how far round the circle it goes along the fixture — 100% is once round. The 100%, 200%, 300% and 400% buttons under Span set it directly, and 100% puts it back to the default. Only Intensity is left below, because the rainbow decides the color

REVERSE swaps the ends, the colors or the direction. MIRROR makes the pattern symmetrical, with the same color at both ends; it does not work with ALTERNATE. SHIFT − and SHIFT + move the pattern one pixel, and the pixel pushed off one end comes back at the other. None of these appear on SOLID.

The row of dots is the first selected fixture's pixels, or every fixture's under ACROSS, read from what is going out. Tap a dot to set that pixel alone with the controls below, and tap it again or ALL to go back. Setting START or END again redraws the blend, pixels set by hand included.

With several fixtures, each takes the same pattern from its own first pixel — that is EACH. ACROSS joins them into one line in their order on Home, from the first pixel of the first fixture to the last pixel of the last. The pattern follows the pixel numbers, so a fixture with inverted pixels (chapter 06) starts from the same side on stage; its own dots show START on the right.

＋ saves the pattern and its colors as a palette and asks for a name. Tap a palette to apply it, and hold it to rename or delete it. Palettes are kept per model on this device, and one made on 16 pixels fits a fixture with 4. The shift and ACROSS are not part of it. With different models selected, the palette row is not there.

Fixtures with Lock on and fixtures running a color effect are left as they are. A Scene stores the colors like any other.

FIXTURES — one fixture as one step

Select two or more fixtures of the same model in the same mode, with PIXELS closed, and the GRADIENT tab shows the same section under FIXTURES. Each fixture is one step, in their order on Home, and there is no EACH or ACROSS. SOLID gives them all the first fixture's color. Setting a fixture's color here clears its own pixel colors, so the fixture's color shows. Palettes are shared with the pixel section of the same model.

While a color effect is running

A color effect — RAINBOW, the colored fires, lightning and fluorescents — runs on any fixture that can make color, whatever mode it is in: RGB, CMY, Hue and Saturation, or xy.

While one runs, the color controls for that fixture are there to read, not to touch. A band at the top of the panel carries a dot lit in the color going out and the name of the effect, and says the color cannot be edited. Intensity still works. The values under the band are the color that comes back when the effect stops, so they stay where you left them.

A mode with no color, or an effect that does not move color, leaves the color controls working as usual.

The band also carries the values going out at this moment. Hold the round fixture icon to open this panel and read them.

06 Per-fixture settings

Limits, Lock and the raw channels of a single fixture.

Scroll down in the panel you get from holding a fixture icon, from COLOR, or from holding a model or group button.

Limits, Lock, Power Switch, BATTERY SAVE and Switch can be set for several fixtures at once. Mixed values show in amber, as — or n of m (for Switch, n of m set as Switch), and changing one applies it to all of them. Channels, Mode, Channel Roles and Patch appear only with a single fixture open. The panel opened from a fixture in the Patch tab has BATTERY SAVE, Switch, the Invert rows, the limits and Label Color below the Re-patch button, but no Lock, Power Switch or Channels; those are in the panel from holding the fixture's icon. On a panel for selected pixels, the limits change only those pixels and there is no Switch; Lock, Power Switch, BATTERY SAVE and Label Color act on the whole fixture.

Name and display

The title at the top of the panel is read-only: the fixture number and the name shown under the faders. Below it, under Skip BATTERY SAVE when that is showing, two lines name the fixture. Label is the display name every fixture of the same model in the same mode shares; change it and they all change, while a fixture in another mode keeps its own Label. It starts as the name from Patch; clear the field and the model's own name shows faintly in it, and when you commit the empty field the model's name comes back. Name belongs to this fixture alone; leave it empty and the Label is shown. Under the faders, in titles and in the large readout, a fixture shows its Name if it has one, and its Label if not. In the panel opened from the Patch tab, or by holding a fixture's round icon on Home, ‹ and › move to the previous or next fixture. They do not appear on a cell's panel or on a panel for several fixtures. In the panel from the Patch tab, Re-patch turns the title into a field for the fixture's name in Patch, the name the patch lists show. Label Color is the background of the number. No label color clears it.

Limits

Lower Limit and Upper Limit set the range you can work in. Change them with ±1 and ±5, or clear them. Outside a limit, Home shows orange hatching.

A cell's limits apply inside the body's. If the body is capped at 50, a cell capped at 80 still cannot pass 50.

Lock

WARNING

Fixture Lock holds a fixture's output where it is. The grand master, blackout, BATTERY SAVE, MIDI, the session and Scene recalls do not change it — a locked fixture will not go out when you press blackout. Check your locks before a take.

With Lock on, the fixture's output is held. Faders, piano mode, ⏻, color, raw channels, GM, B.O., BATTERY SAVE, MIDI and the session all leave it alone, and so do Scene recalls.

Lock holds the DMX values at the fixture's addresses just before they go out; unlocking returns them to the current values. If a locked fixture's address or mode changes, or it is deleted, the old addresses keep sending the held values, and a red note in the Patch section says so. A lock left without its fixture appears in DMX Monitor, where UNLOCK releases it. Locks are saved in the show. An effect on a locked fixture stops where it was when you locked it.

Locks and limits belong to the console, not to a Scene. No Scene records them, and a recall never locks, unlocks or moves a locked fixture. Unlock it and nothing moves: it keeps the values it had, and takes a Scene's values from the next recall. Lock This Scene is a different thing (chapter 08), and chapter 08 covers what a Scene stores.

With several fixtures selected and some of them locked, tapping clears every lock. With none locked, tapping locks them all.

Locking during a piano, FLASH or HIT press puts the temporary value back first, then holds. Changing limits while locked does not move the current value; it is brought into the new range when you unlock.

The other settings

ItemWhat it is
Power SwitchWhat ⏻ does: NONE, ON/OFF, FLASH ON, FLASH OFF or LOCK. ON/OFF is the default. LOCK makes each press lock or unlock the fixture
BATTERY SAVEMarks this fixture for BATTERY SAVE. While BATTERY SAVE is on, Skip BATTERY SAVE at the top of the panel brings a marked fixture back to its fader level until BATTERY SAVE is turned off, with the amount cut shown beside it
Invert Pixels / Invert Pan / Invert TiltInvert Pan and Invert Tilt reverse the direction of Move effects on this fixture only. Invert Pixels reverses the order of this fixture's pixels, and its pixel faders on Home mirror with it
SwitchTurns this fader into an ON / OFF switch (chapter 04). Not the same as Power Switch, which sets what ⏻ does
ModeShows the current DMX mode. Change beside it opens Re-patch at the mode list
Channel RolesCorrects the role and name of each channel. Addresses do not move

Use Channel Roles when a patched fixture has channels being treated as the wrong function. To carry the fix into fixtures you patch later, edit the definition under Custom Fixtures instead.

Channels — the raw DMX (Advanced)

Use the dedicated controls for color, position and the rest first. Channels is for reaching functions those controls do not cover, one DMX channel at a time.

Channels lists everything in DMX order, under Dimmer, Color, Position, Gobo, Beam, Focus, Shapers and Control. Empty groups are hidden.

Kind of rowHow to work it
A continuous valueSlider, typing, or − and +
Named values and rangesA menu up to 12 entries, a searchable list beyond that
Commands like Reset or Lamp OffHold for the stated time. Let go early to cancel. Commands with no time are a tap
A row marked FADER or COLORDriven by a dedicated control. Where the console has a knob for it, such as CCT or G/M, the row carries a slider and a number field to edit it here; where it has none, such as white or strobe, the row is only a label
A row that depends on another channelShows what is available in the current state. When the row is not in use, a note names the channel and the range that switch it off

On a fixture whose second light source has its own dimmer, such as the Aura ring of a MAC Aura XIP, that dimmer is a row of its own here. The fader scales it: what goes out is the row's value times the fader, so with the fader at 0 it is dark. Intensity effects do not move it. B.O., GM and BATTERY SAVE act on it as well.

DMX at the top right switches between raw values and percentages. Home on a row returns it to its default; on Pan and Tilt that needs a hold. It is unavailable when nothing has been changed.

Changes to raw channels are recorded in HISTORY. Whether they also go into the current Scene follows chapter 08: AUTO UPDATE writes them as you work, MANUAL UPDATE waits for UPDATE, and a Scene with Lock This Scene on records nothing. On a pixel fixture, the body panel carries the body channels and a cell panel carries that cell's.

Changing the patch or the mode

Edit from Re-patch in the Patch section. You can see and change the universe and address, fixture number, model and mode. Channel Roles and Delete This Fixture are there too, and the settings under it are hidden while it is open. Next Free moves it to the next gap. Each change here is one step in HISTORY.

Change Mode shows the range before and after and any fixtures it would overlap, before you confirm. Apply to all changes every fixture of the same product that is in the same mode as this one; fixtures in another mode are left as they are. Fixtures after it do not move on their own. When the new mode would overlap or run past channel 512, Change & Move to Next Free also appears, with Move to showing where it goes. Kanau changes only its own patch: set each fixture's own DMX address to its Move to value.

Delete This Fixture removes it from the patch after a confirmation, not only from a group, along with its values and settings, and takes it out of every Scene. HISTORY can undo it.

07 Position and beam

Pan, tilt, zoom, iris, frost and gobo on moving lights.

Pan and Tilt

Hold a fixture's round icon to open its panel, then switch to MOVE at the top. The switch is there whenever the selection holds a fixture with head or optics rows, and the side you left it on is the side that opens next time. A fixture with only strobe or effect channels has no MOVE; its rows stay under Channels (chapter 06), and it opens on DIM / COLOR. MOVE works on everything you have selected: the rows are grouped by model and mode, a value the whole group shares is shown, and where they differ it reads —.

% and DMX at the top of the MOVE face, beside the name of what you have open, switch between the fixture's own units and the raw DMX number. It is the same switch as the one under Channels and in the DMX monitor, so the whole console follows it. On DMX a field reads 0–255, or 0–65535 where the row is 16-bit.

Pan and Tilt read in degrees where the fixture data carries angles, and in percent where it does not. On a 16-bit fixture, coarse and fine sit on one row.

  • Drag near the handle and it moves by the distance your finger travels. Anywhere else scrolls the panel.
  • Type an angle into the field. Values outside the fixture's range are refused.
  • Step with ±0.1°, ±1°, ±10° and so on. The steps come from the unit and the resolution.
  • Hold Home to send it to the fixture's own start position. Let go early to cancel.

With more than one fixture selected and their values apart, the slider and the step keys move them all by the same amount. The gaps between them are kept, and the ones that reach an end stop there while the rest carry on. Typing a value, Home, and picking from a list still put every fixture on the same value.

FAN sits on the Pan and Tilt rows whenever more than one fixture is selected. Turn it on and the slider becomes how far open they are: the middle stays where it is and the two ends open out by the same amount, reading ±n°. Turn it off and the slider goes back to moving them together.

Invert Pan and Invert Tilt reverse the direction of Move effects on this fixture only; the slider and the angle it shows are not reversed. Nothing moves while the fixture is locked.

Dead ranges, where the DMX value does nothing, are skipped by both the slider and the steps. On a fixture whose default sits inside a dead range, the steps will not move: use the slider or type a value to get into the live range first.

Position is recorded in HISTORY. Whether it also goes into the current Scene follows chapter 08: AUTO UPDATE writes it as you work, MANUAL UPDATE waits for UPDATE, and a Scene with Lock This Scene on records nothing.

IMPORTANT

A Scene fade moves Pan, Tilt and the optics. They travel over the fade time the same way intensity does. What still switches the moment you recall is the values you choose rather than dial — gobo, prism, an animation wheel — and anything set in seconds or hertz. Chapter 08 has the list.

Zoom, iris, frost, focus and gobo

MOVE carries Position, Gobo, Beam, Focus and Shapers. A continuous value has a slider with the word for each end under it, step keys, and a field to type into. A named choice — a gobo, a prism, an animation wheel — sits between two arrow keys that walk the list one at a time, and a long list carries a magnifier to search. Home beside a row sends that one channel to the fixture's own start position. Anything outside these shelves is still under Channels (chapter 06).

To animate any of it, use Move and Beam in the EFFECT panel. Move works around wherever the head is pointing now, and layers on top of intensity effects.

Named looks

Each shelf — Position, Gobo, Beam, Focus and Shapers — carries its own row of named looks under its heading, with SAVE at the end of the row. A look holds its own value for each fixture, not one value shared by all of them.

  1. Select the fixtures and set them the way you want them.
  2. Tap SAVE. A Name box opens with a name already in it, such as POSITION 1.
  3. Tap SAVE again, or change the name first.

SAVE is only there while the selection holds a fixture with rows on that shelf.

Tapping a name puts the stored values back. It goes to the fixtures you have selected that are in that look; with nothing selected it goes to every fixture in it. A fixture that is not in the look is left alone, and so is one now in a different DMX mode from the one it was saved in.

Hold a name for Rename, Update — which writes what is set now into it — and Delete.

The looks belong to the show, not to a Scene. Tapping one puts the values there at once; store them in a Scene if you want them to travel over a fade time.
