08 Storing and recalling looks — Scenes

A Scene is a stored look. Open Scenes, tap SAVE to store, tap a row to bring it back.

Storing a Scene

  1. Set intensity, color and any effects on Home.
  2. Tap Scenes → SAVE. It is stored straight away and becomes the current Scene. While a fade is running, from GO until it has landed, SAVE is dim and stores nothing.
  3. To rename it, tap Settings on that Scene's row and type a name.
  4. To protect what is in it, turn on Lock This Scene in the same panel.

The Settings here is the one inside the Scene's row. It is not the Settings tab at the bottom of the screen.

SAVE names a new Scene with the whole number after the last numbered one in the list: after 1, 1.1 and 2 it is 3, and with none it is 1. A name is 8 characters at most; a number at its start, such as 12 or 1.25 followed by a space, does not count toward the 8.

When your changes are recorded

Two buttons at the top of Scenes decide this, and a line under them says what the one you picked does. Until a Scene has been recalled or stored with SAVE, nothing is recorded, and the line says so; the same when the recalled Scene is locked. The choice is kept in the show file rather than on the phone, so a finished show opens the way you left it.

ButtonWhat happens once you have recalled a Scene
AUTO UPDATEEverything you then do to the light is recorded into that Scene as you lift your finger. There is nothing to press
MANUAL UPDATENothing is recorded until you tap UPDATE. Recalling another Scene throws away what you have not recorded, and does not ask

Switching between the two records nothing by itself. Going from MANUAL UPDATE to AUTO UPDATE does not write what is already waiting; AUTO UPDATE starts from your next move.

Under the current Scene's row, a strip says which of these is happening. The strip stays in the same position, and its label and appearance show whether UPDATE can be pressed.

StripWhenTap
LOCKED, greenThe Scene is locked, under either buttonNo
● RECORDING, the dot red and breathingAUTO UPDATE, not lockedNo. It is saying that what you do now is going in
UPDATE, dimMANUAL UPDATE, nothing differs from the recallNo
UPDATE, bright and blinkingMANUAL UPDATE, something differsYes. Records the current state

Under MANUAL UPDATE the difference is measured against the moment of the recall, or of storing it with SAVE. Take a fader to 30 and back to 50 and there is nothing left to record. While a fade is running, only what you touch is counted, and it goes into the Scene the fade is heading for; values the fade itself is moving are never counted. A FLASH, piano key or HIT you are holding is not recorded; SAVE, UPDATE and AUTO UPDATE take the look with your finger off. Lifting your finger from the ZEN fader, or switching TILT off, counts as letting go of a fader.

What a Scene has recorded is not part of HISTORY.

Recalling and tidying

A recall brings back GM and B.O. as well, so it can raise the grand master or clear a blackout.

There is no way to read what a Scene has stored before you recall it. Its Settings hold the name, the Delay, the fade time, the Curve, Fixture Times, the lock and Delete, and nothing else. Watching the GM figure at the top of the screen tells you what the value is now, not what the Scene will put there.

Stepping back repairs a recall; it does not stand in for checking first. The recall counts as one step in HISTORY, and stepping back restores GM and B.O. with everything else — only locks are never undone (chapter 10) — but by then the light has already moved, on stage as well as on screen.

What does keep a fixture out of a recall is Fixture Lock; a Scene never changes a lock (chapter 10); how fast the change is seen depends on what it is — the Fade section below says which values travel over the fade time and which switch at once.

Action or markWhat it does
Tap a rowRecalls when you lift your finger. While Select Many is on, it selects the row instead
NEXT / BACKThe next or previous Scene. It wraps around. Unavailable with only one Scene
● and an amber backgroundThe current Scene
▸The Scene NEXT will bring up. Shown only while a Scene is recalled
LOCKED and a green edgeLocked against recording
SettingsName, Delay, fade time, Curve, Fixture Times, lock, delete
STAGEOpens the full-screen page for sending Scenes on the night. Shown only with two or more Scenes
Select ManyAt the right edge, under BACK / NEXT. Reorder, and select rows for Copy or Delete. It turns into Done. Not shown while BLIND is on, nor to a guest that cannot touch Scenes
RENUMBERJust left of Select Many. Asks Renumber Scenes?, then with Renumber All numbers every Scene 1, 2, 3 and so on in list order. Not shown while BLIND is on, nor to a guest
CopyCopies each selected Scene to just after itself and any copies already made from it
DeleteAsks first. Copy does not, because nothing is lost. A deleted Scene's MIDI Note goes with it

The numbers are display order. The time under the name is when its contents last changed. At the right of a row is its fade time, such as 3.0s. When some fixtures have times of their own, or the Scene has a Delay, a second line below it, such as / 7.0s, says how long until the last fixture has arrived. While a Scene is coming in, a bar under its row runs pale through the Delay, then amber over the fade.

On iPad the row of buttons along the bottom of Home ends with the Scenes: a lock key, the current Scene's name with NEXT → and the next one under it, BACK and NEXT side by side, and UPDATE. With no Scene yet it is a grey place that reads Scenes you save will appear here. BACK and NEXT do what they do in this panel, and UPDATE reads like the strip under the current Scene's row — LOCKED, RECORDING or UPDATE. Tap RECORDING, or a dim UPDATE, to choose AUTO UPDATE or MANUAL UPDATE from a short list; not while BLIND is on. While a Scene fades in, a thin line along the bottom of the name runs pale through the Delay, then amber over the Fade. The row is locked each time Kanau opens, with a cover over it from the key to UPDATE: slide the slider on the cover to the right to unlock, and tap the key to lock it again. Touching the covered row only shakes it. Strap Lock locks it as well, and unlocking Strap Lock leaves it locked.

A copy is named after its source's number with one more decimal: 1 gives 1.1, then 1.2 up to 1.9; 1.1 gives 1.11. Only the number is carried, not the rest of the name, and a source with no number gives the next free whole number. A copy keeps the contents, the Delay, the fade time, the Curve and Fixture Times, and is never locked, even when the one it came from is. The copies become the selected rows, so pressing Copy again copies the copies.

RENUMBER changes names only. The number goes in front of the name, so Opening becomes 1 Opening, or takes the place of a number already there, so 1.1 Toast becomes 2 Toast; an empty name becomes the number alone. The order, the current Scene and what is recorded stay as they are. The old numbers cannot be brought back, and HISTORY does not hold them.

STAGE — sending Scenes on the night

STAGE is a full-screen page for sending Scenes during the show, on a black ground. Tap STAGE in the title row of Scenes, to the left of SAVE. It is shown only when there are two or more Scenes and BLIND is off. A guest in a session that can only watch does not see it.

PartWhat it does
Settings mark, top rightOpens STAGE settings, described under this table
×, top leftLeaves STAGE and returns to Scenes
The name above NEXTThe current Scene, written large, with an amber ● at its left while a Scene is recalled. Until a Scene is recalled it reads —
NEXT and BACKThe two large buttons. Inside NEXT, ▸ and the next Scene's name with its fade time (3.0s, or 3.0s / 7.0s when the Scene has Fixture Times); inside BACK, ◂ and the previous Scene's. You can see where each goes before you press it. BACK is half as tall as NEXT, and as wide

The mark at the top right opens STAGE settings, with Done at its top right. Buttons chooses NEXT or BACK + NEXT. With NEXT, the whole page below the name is one NEXT button. With BACK + NEXT, BACK is above NEXT. The choice is kept on this device, and BACK + NEXT is where it starts. Fade sets the six fade buttons: tap one, then change its time with −1, −0.1, +0.1 and +1, within the same range as a Scene's own fade. A time of 0 reads SNAP. The six buttons are not on STAGE itself; they appear in each Scene's Settings → Fade, where pressing one sets that Scene's fade. A guest that cannot touch Scenes does not see Fade.

The Scene goes out when you lift your finger, so sliding off a button before you let go sends nothing. After the last Scene, NEXT goes round to the first, with a warning haptic. A press within 0.5 seconds of the one before is refused, with the same warning haptic, so a hand that lands twice does not send two Scenes. While STAGE is open the screen does not lock itself, neither by tilting the phone nor by iOS.

BLIND — working without touching the lights

BLIND, the wide button under the title of Scenes, starts a copy of the console that sends nothing. A line under it says what it does; while BLIND is on, the button is amber with a light running along it. It starts from the faders, colors and effects as they are, or from where a running fade is heading. The lights keep doing what they were doing.

While BLIND is on, faders, color, effects and Scene recalls change the copy only; GM and B.O. still act on the lights. The band at the top, the edge of the screen and each panel are marked in amber. SAVE stores the BLIND look as a new Scene and UPDATE writes it into the current one; on iPhone UPDATE is also on Home, in the place of BATTERY SAVE, and now and then shows the current Scene's name; AUTO UPDATE and MANUAL UPDATE are not shown, and BLIND always records the way MANUAL UPDATE does. Patch, Output, Session, Shows, HISTORY and Scene settings are closed, and in a fixture's panel the name cannot be typed and Label Color, BATTERY SAVE, Invert and Switch are hidden. Nothing you do in BLIND goes into HISTORY. The one exception is reordering the faders with REORDER on Home, which stays open: it changes the order of the show itself, not only of the copy, and its move is a step in HISTORY.

To leave, tap BLIND again, or BLIND at the top left of the screen. With unsaved changes it asks Update, Save New, Discard or Cancel. Leaving never changes the lights. A guest in a session has no BLIND.

Scene Lock

Turn on Lock This Scene for Scenes you want left alone. You can still recall them and still work the light, but nothing is recorded. LOCKED is shown on every locked row, not only on the current one.

Lock is stronger than either update button. A locked Scene never says RECORDING.

This is not the same as Fixture Lock. Scene Lock protects what is stored; Fixture Lock holds the output.

What is stored, and what is not

A Scene stores the intensities and colors, and with them settings such as GM and B.O. The table below says exactly what.

Stored and brought backNot stored
Intensity, CCT, G/M, crossfade, RGB, emitters, the name of the gel picked from a tableBATTERY SAVE
Raw channels such as position and gobo, cell color and intensity, effectsPower Switch
Color groups, ⏻ state, GM and B.O.Limits and Fixture Lock

Locks and limits belong to the console, not to a Scene. A Scene does not record them and a recall does not apply them, so a recall never locks, unlocks or re-limits a fixture, and the console's limits hold the light of every Scene. A locked fixture is not written into a Scene either: AUTO UPDATE and UPDATE leave the value the Scene already has, and SAVE takes its present value. Unlock it and nothing moves; the next recall brings in the Scene's value.

Fade

Set it per Scene in Settings → Fade. 3 seconds is the default. There are six preset buttons, at first SNAP, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2 and 3, and ±0.1 and ±1 to adjust. The times of the six buttons are chosen in STAGE settings (Scenes → STAGE → the settings mark). The value beside the heading can also be typed: tap it, type the seconds on the number keys and press Return. The range is the same as the ± buttons, 0 to 600 seconds in steps of 0.1, so typing 700 gives 600. Something that cannot be read as a number changes nothing.

The Scene's Settings open over the whole screen, with × at the top left. At the top, a bar shows the Delay as a dotted line and the Fade after it: drag the knob where they meet for the Delay and the one at the end for the Fade, in steps of 0.1 seconds. Delay, under the bar, is how long the whole Scene waits after GO before anything moves. It is 0 unless you set it, has the same ± keys and can be typed, but has no preset buttons. Curve, under Fade, sets how the fade moves: S-CURVE, the default, starts and lands gently; EASE IN starts gently only; LINEAR moves at one even speed. Settings → Settings → Fade Times → Scene Curve sets it for every Scene at once, and for Scenes saved from now on.

Intensity, color, cell values, color groups and GM travel over the fade time, and so do Pan, Tilt and the continuous beam values such as Zoom, Focus and Iris, following the Scene's Curve. That includes Amber, White, Lime, the fixture's own Hue and Saturation, x and y, and CMY; hue goes the short way round the circle. The faders move with them. What you touch part-way — with a fader, ⏻, color or a MIDI knob, or from the guest in a session — leaves the fade and stays where you put it, while the fixture's other values carry on; just taking hold of a fader is enough. Under AUTO UPDATE what you touched goes into the Scene the fade is heading for at once; under MANUAL UPDATE, UPDATE lights. A piano key or FLASH gives its value while held and is not recorded; let go and the fixture stops at the value it had before you pressed, then goes to the Scene's value when the fade lands. A key still held when the fade lands goes to the Scene's value when you let go.

B.O., ⏻, a fader set as a switch and the name of the gel do not interpolate, and neither do the raw values that are chosen rather than dialled: gobo, prism, an animation wheel, and anything set in seconds or hertz. They switch to the stored value the moment you recall, whatever the fade time says; B.O. waits for the Scene's Delay first. An effect you start, stop or change during the fade is yours and stays as you set it. Where you are coming from holds no position at all — an older Scene, for example — the head lands on the new value at once.

Effects cross over with the fade, along the Scene's Curve. An effect the Scene brings starts when its fixture starts to move and grows from nothing over that fixture's Fade; one the Scene does not have keeps running while it fades out, and is released when the fade lands; where both have one, the light passes from the old to the new. An effect that plays once, ONE FIRE, the SIGNAL crossings and a recall with a fade of 0 switch at once. For a fixture that has a Delay (see Fixture Times below), effects reach it when its Delay ends.

The recall itself is recorded in HISTORY as one step. Scenes are part of the show file.

Fixture Times — a different time for each fixture

Every fixture follows the Scene's Fade unless you say otherwise. Fixture Times, in the Scene's Settings below Fade, lets chosen fixtures start at a time of their own, counted from GO (Delay), or take their own time to get there (Fade), so a look can build across the stage. The section is not shown while there are no fixtures. A fixture you have not set follows the Scene's Delay and Fade; one set to a Delay of 0 starts at GO even when the Scene has a Delay.

Beside the heading, in amber, is the time until the last fixture has arrived: the longest Delay plus Fade among the fixtures. A short explanation and a scale in seconds follow, then one row for each fixture, in fader order, with its number in thin type, its name and a bar. The name sits on the fixture's Label Color when it has one. A dotted line is the Delay, and the bar after it is the Fade. A Fade of 0 shows as a thin vertical mark where the fixture starts. The bar is stronger for a fixture that has a time of its own and paler for one that follows the Scene's Fade. The scale is fixed by the Scene's Fade: the width you can see holds at least 5 seconds, and at least twice the Scene's Fade. Giving one fixture a long Delay or Fade does not shrink the bars of the others; only the bar of the long fixture grows. What runs past the edge is seen by sliding the band, the scale and all the bars together, sideways with a finger. The column of names stays still. The time beside the heading is still when the last fixture has arrived.

Drag the knob at the start of a fixture's bar to set its Delay, and the one at the end to set its Fade; it then has times of its own, and touching a knob without moving it changes nothing. With groups in the patch, ALL and a button for each group under the explanation narrow the rows. Tap a row to select it, and tap it again to let it go; pressing another group button lets go of the rows it hides. A selected row has a thick amber edge. While anything is selected, a bar appears at the bottom of the panel: the number selected out of all the fixtures, RESET and CLEAR, and a line each for Delay and Fade. Each line shows the value of the selected fixtures, or — when they differ. −1, −0.1, +0.1 and +1 change every selected fixture by that much from its own present value, so the differences between them stay. Delay and Fade stay within the same range as the Scene's own Fade. Tap the value on the Delay or Fade line to type it: the number keys open, and Return gives every selected fixture exactly that number, not a step from its own value. Something that cannot be read as a number changes nothing. RESET sends the selected fixtures back to the Scene's Delay and Fade. CLEAR lets go of every selected row, as CLEAR does on Home: the bottom bar closes and the times stay as they are.

On a recall, a fixture that has a Delay stays as it was until its Delay ends, then moves over its own Fade. The Scene's effects come to each fixture at the moment it starts. Repeating effects on the light keep time with the recall, so fixtures that started late still blink and chase in step; effects on position and beam, and effects that play once, begin from rest at the moment that fixture starts. GM waits for the Scene's Delay, then travels over the Scene's Fade, or over the time left if that is shorter. B.O. and SIGNAL crossings switch when the Scene's Delay ends, at once when there is none. Touch GM or B.O. while they wait and yours stands.

What you touch on a fixture that is still waiting leaves the fade and stays as you set it. An effect you change during the fade is not overwritten when a waiting fixture's Delay ends.

09 Effects

Blink, fire, lightning and the rest, applied to your fixtures.

EFFECT on Home applies an effect to what you have selected. From the Effects tab you can also tap the effect first and pick its fixtures next; on Home, EFFECT needs a selection. The Effects tab at the bottom opens the same panel with EFFECT, and it is where everything that is running is managed.

Applying one

  1. On Home, tap the round icon of a fixture or a cell to select it.
  2. Open EFFECT.
  3. Tap an effect name. It starts immediately.

With nothing selected the names are still live. Tap one and a panel opens under that name to pick its fixtures; Done starts it. Cancel, or pulling the panel down, starts nothing.

The fader still sets intensity. While an effect runs, the EFFECT button carries its name when its fixtures are selected, and reads N RUNNING, such as 2 RUNNING, when nothing is selected; the fixture icon and fader move with it. On a fader set as a switch, intensity effects do nothing; color effects still change its color.

At the top of the panel, a round icon stands for each step: the color of the light source in it, its number in the order underneath (not the fixture number), and the movement it is actually making. A step with nothing in it is a faint ring carrying +, and it stays dark as the chase goes past. The band above them shows the shape over time — in the effect's own color when it carries one, and plain when it does not.

Under the icons sit three keys: TOGETHER, SPREAD and STEPS. TOGETHER moves every light source as one; SPREAD gives each its own place in the run. Whichever is lit is the state, and with nothing selected both go dim and refuse. STEPS lights as well once you have set the seats by hand. The movement and the seats are two different things, so two keys can be lit at once and SPREAD over three steps reads as both. On the seats the app deals out itself, STEPS stays dark. RUNNER, FADE RUN and COMET always run apart.

STEPS opens the room where the steps live. It covers every fixture running that effect, not only the ones selected, so a change to the steps keeps the whole chase in step. Each step is a row with what is in it — Empty when there is nothing — and a SELECT of its own; + ADD STEP puts one on the end; EDIT brings out the handles, and a row dragged by its handle moves to another place in the order. Swipe a row to the left for DELETE. One step is the fewest there can be — and one step is TOGETHER.

Tapping an empty step opens the fixture list — the same one the step list's SELECT opens, with whatever is already in that step ticked. Tick to put a fixture in, untick to take it out. Done writes it; Cancel, or pulling the panel down, leaves the step as it was.

Tap the icons to pick out fixtures; the row under them says how many are MARKED, with ALL to mark every one and CLEAR to let them go. An icon marked … opens that fixture's own color and intensity panel on a hold — the same panel as the round icon on Home. Hold with several picked out and they open together.

Pause, release, restart

ActionWhat it does
BACKGoes back one step. With TOGETHER it goes back a whole cycle
NEXTGoes on one step, the same way
PAUSEFreezes the movement at the current intensity and position
RESUMECarries on from where it froze
RELEASEStops it and hands control back to the normal values. The settings stay in the list
STARTRuns a released effect again from the beginning
CLEARRemoves it from the list. It asks first

BACK and NEXT are the two arrow keys at the left of the row. They move while the effect is paused as well, so you can walk through it a step at a time. While something runs, the key at the right of the row says RELEASE; once it is stopped the same key says START, so the effect can be set going again without leaving the panel.

Adjust

ItemWhat it is
SpeedIn hertz. Decimals allowed
DepthHow far down it pulls the intensity. 100 reaches zero; 35 barely moves
SizeOn the kinds that move the head, in place of Depth: how far it swings, in degrees per axis. ±25.2° / ±12.6° swings both ways, 0–45° goes one way, and a single moving axis is named, as in Pan 0–90°. The biggest shapes reach ±90°. FINE beside it works like FINE on Home
How OftenHow often it happens. The same knob reads Shape on ORBIT, Crossing Time on PASS and Saturation on RAINBOW. Only on the kinds that use it
RoughnessHow ragged the wander is, on CANDLE, BONFIRE, WATER, LANTERNS, DRIFT, HANDHELD, WIND and BALLYHOO
WidthHow much of the rig is lit at once, for example 50% 2 / 4. On one fixture, or with TOGETHER, how long each beat stays lit; above 50%, PULSE and FADE RUN hold flat at the top
TailThe length of COMET's tail
RandomHow much the beat and the height wander. 0 keeps it regular
DramaOn the two fires. 0 is the real thing; higher makes it a stage fire

Which items appear depends on the effect. SIGNAL has a panel of its own instead.

Arrange

Arrange opens with how the effect treats color; the arrangement sits under it. The kinds that only move the head or the beam carry no color row.

ColorWhat it does
AUTOThe effect decides. The ones that carry no color of their own leave yours alone
COLORIt runs in the colors you set below. A color appears even on the kinds that have none
KEEPOnly the brightness moves. The color stays as you set it on the fader
ArrangementWhat it does
IN ORDEREvenly staggered by number
ALTERNATEOdd and even, half a cycle apart
WINGSMirrored out from the center
RANDOMIn a random order
BOUNCETurns around at each end
BUILDLights one at a time, then clears them all together
SPELLERLights one at a time, and once they are all on, everything flashes together three times
PASSLike IN ORDER, but fast through the middle and slow at the ends, the way a car goes past

Some kinds put a key in Arrange that only works while you hold it. CANDLE and BONFIRE carry FLARE and WIND — hold FLARE to make the fire flare up, WIND to let a gust beat it down. FLUO FLICKER, FLUO DROPOUT, FLUO RESTART and FLUO DYING carry HIT: hold it and the tube fails, let go and it comes back. With CANDLE or BONFIRE on two or more fixtures, Arrange also carries ONE FIRE: the fixtures burn as one big flame, its rise and fall reaching each a little later along their order while each keeps its own flicker. It turns TOGETHER off. On all four, How Often above sets how often the tube fails on its own; at 0 it fails only while HIT is held.

Runs under IN ORDER is how many patterns run at once, set with − n +. It will not go past the number of fixtures you have selected. Direction is FORWARD or REVERSE.

STEPS says how many steps the chase is running over, and how your fixtures or pixels are dealt into them: more fixtures than steps and a step holds several, more steps than fixtures and the spare ones stay dark. Press STEPS above to change how many there are, and which fixture sits in which.

INVERT swaps the lit and the dark. One step lighting up becomes one step going out, and a chase that fills becomes one that empties.

REPEAT on keeps the effect going round. Off, it runs once and holds its last look; press it again to run from the start.

The arrangement, Runs, STEPS and Direction only appear while SPREAD is on, and only on the kinds that run along the rig. INVERT and REPEAT sit outside that: REPEAT is always there, and INVERT on every kind but RAINBOW.

Both work with TOGETHER as well. Invert a blink set to 20% width and you get a short dip in an otherwise bright look; invert STROBE and you get short blackouts inside the light; turn REPEAT off and you get one flash that holds where it ends.

ADVANCED

Every effect carries an ADVANCED section below Arrange. It stays folded until you open it, and the folded heading says EDITED once you have changed something. RESET returns the settings inside ADVANCED to their starting values, and leaves everything above it alone.

BlockOnWhat you change
ColorsBeacons, PACHINKO, FIREWORKSEach lamp or flash, by name — RED, BLUE, AMBER and the rest
FROM / TOTOKYO, OSAKA, KYOTO, NARAThe two ends of the range the street drifts between. Set both the same and the hue goes the whole way round
FAR / NEARLIGHTNINGThe far strike and the near one
TemperatureCANDLE, BONFIRELOW and HIGH in kelvin, in steps of 50
MAXFLUO DYING, CANDLE, BONFIREHow hard the tube fails while HIT is held, or how strongly FLARE and WIND act. 10 to 100%, in steps of 10

This is where you change a fire's own color, because on AUTO it works that color out from its temperature.

The towns — TOKYO, OSAKA, KYOTO, NARA

The four towns differ in character, and each has moments of its own that come now and then. Speed on the towns goes up to 3 Hz.

TownWhat it does
TOKYOMany colors, moving fast. Now and then every sign cuts to one color, or the screens flash white
OSAKAStrong primaries, switching hard. Now and then every sign blinks three times
KYOTOWarm and muted. Lanterns, moving slowly. A breeze passes along the row, and now and then someone walks past a light
NARAThe dimmest. Stone lanterns, barely moving. Now and then a cloud dims them all, or one lantern is relit

Each time you apply a town it is a different night. Stop it and press it again, or apply it from a Saved card, and the time of the special moments, the colors it switches to, the order of the people and fires and the colors the signs drift to all come out differently. The town's character stays the same. A Scene remembers the night it was stored with, and recalling it from a different look starts that same night from the beginning.

Changing the target, and saving settings

Applies To → FIXTURES picks fixtures and groups. The selection is shared with Home, and the list stays open while you choose. A model opens into its fixtures, and a fixture with pixels opens again into ALL PIXELS and P1 … Pn. A fixture goes in whole or by pixel, not both; if both end up chosen, the pixels stay and the whole fixture is let go.

With PIXELS open on Home, selecting a pixel fixture itself and applying an effect works as if you had selected all of its pixels: the arrangement, Runs and Direction play across the pixels, and the panel counts them — 16 selected for one fixture with 16 pixels. With PIXELS closed, each fixture is one step. An effect that is already running is adjusted where it lives, whichever way PIXELS is set.

SAVE, at the top right of the panel, stores the settings you have dialled in, under a name. It is always there. When there is nothing to store, because nothing is running on the selected fixtures or different effects are, it is dimmed and pressing it stores nothing. The Saved row appears once a setting is stored, and says why when the effects are mixed or the stored settings cannot be read. Saved cards are listed under SELECT ▾: pick one to apply it, and pick it again, ticked, to stop. To rename or delete one, open EDIT at the bottom of the list and pick it. Changes made there stay even if you close it by swiping down. An empty name is refused with Enter a name, and the old name stays. The fixtures are not part of a stored setting.

Select the fixtures already running along with the new ones, pick the same effect, and the speed, depth and phase carry over. Where the settings differ, it falls back to the defaults. To release just one fixture, select only that one and RELEASE.

Finding one by what you want

What you wantTry
Natural lightCANDLE, BONFIRE, LIGHTNING, WATER, WIND, TV
Light running along the rigRUNNER, FADE RUN, COMET
City lightNEON, SIGNAL, TOKYO, OSAKA, KYOTO, NARA, PACHINKO
BeaconsBEACON R/B, BEACON BLUE, BEACON RED, BEACON AMBER
Press camerasPAPARAZZI
Plain flashingBLINK, STROBE, PULSE, DOUBLE, JITTER, SPARKLE, RARE FLASH
Color on the moveRAINBOW
A failing fluorescentFLUO FLICKER, FLUO DROPOUT, FLUO RESTART, FLUO DYING
Moving the headThe Move group
Moving zoom or goboThe Beam group
An old signMarquee

PAPARAZZI is camera flashes from a crowd. Each fixture fires on its own and stays dark in between, so the more you give it the less it looks like a pattern. How Often sets how many go off.

The two fires, and the failing tubes

CANDLE is a candle: in still air it sits almost still, and it only moves when something disturbs it. BONFIRE is a bonfire: a fast flicker around 2.7 Hz, with a gust of wind pushing it down now and then. Speed on BONFIRE goes up to 2.5 Hz.

Drama in Adjust sits on both and starts at 0, which is the real thing. Raise it and the fire becomes a stage fire: it stops going still, it reddens as it drops, and it flickers more than a real one would.

The fires take the color row in Arrange like any other effect. On AUTO they work their own color out from their temperature, and the temperature is under ADVANCED. Pick COLOR instead and they run in the color you set, keeping the flame's shape.

On AUTO, a fire whose fixtures carry both a color temperature channel and color of their own gets CCT and RGB to choose between. The two do not reach the same color. CCT rides the temperature channel, so the light makes the white it was calibrated for and the deepest embers stop at the lowest temperature it can reach. RGB rides the red, green and blue channels, and can paint the deep reds of the embers that a temperature channel cannot. Where a fixture has only one of the two, the choice does not appear.

The first three are a tube that works and now and then goes out: FLUO FLICKER flickers two to four times and comes straight back; FLUO DROPOUT flickers, drops out and lights again at once; FLUO RESTART goes out, the ends glow orange, it misfires and finally lights. They are lit when applied and go out only on HIT or by themselves, as How Often says. FLUO DYING is a tube that tries to light and fails: the ends glow, it flashes, it drops. On a fixture with pixels, only the two ends glow amber.

The full list

GroupEffects
BasicBLINK, STROBE, PULSE, DOUBLE, JITTER, SPARKLE, RARE FLASH, RUNNER, FADE RUN, COMET
LightsFLUO FLICKER, FLUO DROPOUT, FLUO RESTART, FLUO DYING, CANDLE, BONFIRE, LIGHTNING, PAPARAZZI, TV, NEON, SIGNAL
PlacesBEACON R/B, BEACON BLUE, BEACON RED, BEACON AMBER, TOKYO, OSAKA, KYOTO, NARA, PACHINKO, WATER, FIREWORKS, LANTERNS, RAINBOW
MoveDRIFT, PASS, ORBIT, EIGHT, BOX, SPIRAL, SEARCH, BREATHE, HANDHELD, WIND, JUMP, BALLYHOO
BeamZOOM PULSE, ZOOM BREATHE, IRIS PULSE, FROST BREATHE, GOBO SHAKE

RUNNER, FADE RUN and COMET need several fixtures, or pixels. Move and Beam appear when the selected fixtures support them.

An amber dot at the top right of a name means the effect changes color as well. Without the dot, it uses the color you set by hand.

SIGNAL — traffic lights

SIGNAL is a crossing, and its name opens a panel of its own instead of applying anything. A crossing has two roads, and each road carries a light for its cars and one for the people walking alongside it, who get their green together with those cars: CAR · ROAD 1, WALK · ROAD 1, CAR · ROAD 2, WALK · ROAD 2.

Each signal is a card. Inside it sits a round icon for the whole signal, marked ALL, and beside it the lamps in a housing of their own — G Y R for the cars, R G for the people, in the order that country hangs them. An empty circle carries +, and the number of fixtures in the signal is under the name.

To fill a signal, select the fixtures on Home, open SIGNAL and tap an empty circle; a panel opens with them already ticked, and Done puts them in. Tapping a circle with nothing in hand opens the same panel to choose from. The ALL circle takes a fixture that is the whole signal and changes color for every phase; a lamp circle takes fixtures that light only for that lamp. A fixture picked for more than one lamp has its pixels divided between them, and pixels you placed by hand stay where you put them. Such a fixture is listed, ticked, in each lamp's panel; untick it to take it out of that lamp only. One light source lives in one place only.

The two lines at the top say where the crossing stands — ⏸ WAITING · CAR · ROAD 1 · GREEN, with what NEXT will reach underneath and a bar for the run to it. While it runs the first word is RUNNING; between two stops, CHANGING.

ButtonWhat it does
PLAYRuns from where it is. Without REPEAT it stops at the head of the cycle, where ROAD 1 goes
PAUSEHolds where it is, mid-phase if need be
BACKGoes to the previous change
NEXTGoes to the next change
REPEATKeeps the cycle running by itself

A change is any point where a signal that has fixtures in it, and whose button is lit under NEXT STOPS AT, comes to a lamp it can stay on. Yellow, and red with yellow, are passed through. With people lights, their green and their flashing green are changes too. NEXT STOPS AT is the row just above BACK and NEXT, with four buttons: CAR 1, WALK 1, CAR 2 and WALK 2. All four are lit at first. Turn one off and NEXT no longer stops for that signal; it still changes in order and at its real pace, and only the waits in between are cut short. The last lit button does not go off, and the button of a signal with no fixtures is dim and does not light.

Below the buttons sit the country and ADVANCED, with a second key beside it for the signal you are editing: how long each lamp holds, with − 40s +, the color of each lamp, and RESET. One cycle stays 90 seconds — what you add to one phase comes out of the longest one.

SIGNAL 1 ▾ at the top switches between crossings and + NEW adds one. Each crossing keeps its own clock, country and signals.

Opening SIGNAL with fixtures that are in no crossing yet takes you to an empty crossing, and makes a new one when none is empty. Fixtures already in a crossing open that crossing.

Back in the EFFECT panel, when every selected fixture is in a crossing, the top of the panel shows that crossing's two lines, and the row of buttons under it drives that crossing: BACK, NEXT, PLAY or PAUSE, and REPEAT. PAUSE lights amber while the crossing runs, and REPEAT while it is on. Applying an effect takes the fixtures out of the crossing, and the top goes back to the effect. RELEASE ALL lets go of the crossings too: their fixtures go back to their own light, and each crossing keeps its signals and settings. START ALL starts them again from the head of the cycle. A crossing holding a locked fixture is left as it is.

Marquee — the old bulb-sign shapes

Marquee is a row of cards in the panel, just under Basic. They are the shapes an old bulb sign ran, under the names the signs used; pressing one sets the shape and the arrangement together. From there you adjust it with the same knobs as every other effect.

A card does not decide how many steps there are. Pressing one gives you a step for each light source you have selected, and for the dark gaps of a real sign you add steps with + at the head of the icon row. The color arrives as COLOR, set to the warm glow of old tungsten; KEEP runs it in the color you made on the fader instead.

PatternWhat it does
CHASEOne bulb runs along the sign
DARK CHASEAll lit but one, and the dark one runs
CRAWLTwo side by side run together
BOUNCERuns to the end and comes back the way it came
BUILDLights one by one, then all clear together
FILLFills from the front, then empties from the front
FLIP FLOPOdd and even take turns
FLASHAll on, all off
TWINKLEEach bulb blinks on its own
SPELLERSpells out, then flashes three times

DARK CHASE is CHASE with INVERT on, and FILL is BUILD with INVERT on. The same switch turns any of the running shapes inside out.

Speed is in hertz, as everywhere else. Depth is how dark an unlit step goes: below 100 it keeps a little glow, like a filament cooling. Direction, BACK and NEXT work as they do on the rest.

Layering LIGHT, MOVE and BEAM

One fixture can carry a LIGHT effect for intensity and color, a MOVE effect for the head, and a BEAM effect at once. Choosing another effect in the same lane replaces it. Cells take LIGHT only. On a fixture whose second light source has its own dimmer, such as the Aura ring of a MAC Aura XIP, LIGHT moves the main light only.

Opening the panel shows the first running lane, in the order LIGHT, MOVE, BEAM.

Managing them from the Effects tab

EDIT opens an effect's settings in the same panel; ‹ at the top left goes back to the list. Each row has four buttons in fixed places: EDIT, RELEASE or START, PAUSE or RESUME, and CLEAR. While the effect is released, PAUSE is dim and cannot be pressed. A released effect stays in the list, marked RELEASED, and CLEAR still removes it. EDIT, CLEAR and the row's chips act on that row's own lane — the head or the intensity — so a blink and a figure-eight on one fixture stay apart.

n ∨ opens the fixture chips for that row; n ∧ folds them again. The × on a chip drops that one fixture. The + adds what you have selected, a group, a model, or All. RELEASE ALL and START ALL apply to everything. Each crossing has a row of its own — SIGNAL 1, SIGNAL 2 and so on — with EDIT and CLEAR.

Effects keep counting through a blackout. Unlocked fixtures go dark and pick the movement up where it is when you clear it. On a locked fixture the effect stops where it was when you locked it; unlock it and it picks up where the effect has got to. Fixture Lock is covered in chapter 10.

10 Locks, safety and stepping back

What stops you making a mistake in the middle of a take, and what lets you undo one.

There are three kinds of lock

The word turns up in three places, and each protects something different.

NameWhat it protectsWhere
Fixture LockThe fixture's current output. The value cannot changeThe fixture panel
Scene LockWhat is stored in a SceneSettings on the Scene's row
SCREEN LOCKThe screen. Touches do nothingTop of the screen, or Strap Lock

SCREEN LOCK

Hold SCREEN LOCK at the top of the screen for 0.5 seconds. A short tap will not lock it.

While locked, a purple wash and hatching cover the screen. The values stay readable, and sending and fades carry on. To unlock, drag the purple slider in the middle about 80% of the way to the right. Let go early and it stays locked.

SCREEN LOCK is out of reach while a panel such as Patch is open. Strap Lock still locks over one.

Strap Lock locks the screen when the iPhone or iPad hangs upside down from a strap. Lifting it does not unlock it; slide right to unlock, as with SCREEN LOCK. It is on by default on iPhone and off on iPad; switch it in Settings → Settings → SCREEN LOCK. On iPad, upside down means the top of the screen tipping toward the floor, however the iPad is held, and it does not lock if the screen turns with the iPad. With the switch on, three buttons under it set how far the top of the device must tip below level before the screen locks: NORMAL (30°), the default, EASY (20°) and EASIEST (12°). The smaller the angle, the less tilt it takes. It does not lock while a finger is on the screen or just after, while ZEN, STAGE or Settings is open, while the keyboard, a confirmation or a file picker is showing, or when the device lies flat. Over Patch, Scenes, Effects, GM, BATTERY SAVE and MOVE it does lock: the panel stays open underneath and is still there when you unlock, and it cannot be pulled down while locked. Auto Unlock, a switch under the buttons that is off by default, changes the lifting: with it on, the screen unlocks as soon as the device is turned upright, with no slide. It lifts only a lock that Strap Lock put on, not one you set with SCREEN LOCK, and nothing happens while the device lies flat, on its side or face down.

Fixture Lock

WARNING

Fixture Lock holds a fixture's output where it is. The grand master, blackout, BATTERY SAVE, MIDI, the session and changes to the patch do not change it — press blackout and a locked fixture stays lit. The count still lit during a blackout is shown next to the green 🔒 at the top of the screen. A Scene recall does not change it either. Locks and limits belong to the console, and no Scene records or applies them (chapter 08).

Hold a fixture icon and turn on Lock. Use it when a light must not change.

While locked, the round icon shows a green padlock, ⏻ shows a large padlock in its place, and the fader carries green. The number button shows no padlock. Clear it from the fixture panel, and the output returns to the current values. The lock holds the values at the fixture's addresses and is saved with the show. A lock whose fixture has been deleted stays on those addresses; release it with UNLOCK in DMX Monitor.

BATTERY SAVE

Dims only the fixtures you mark, for the waiting around between takes.

  1. Mark them in the fixture settings under BATTERY SAVE, or in Patch → Select Many → Battery. You can also mark them as you patch.
  2. Tap BATTERY SAVE at the top of the screen. The marked fixtures dim.
  3. Tap it again to bring them back.

Hold it to set how far it dims and how long the fade takes. Brightness offers −25%, −50%, −65% and −75%, and −50% is the default. The fade is SNAP, 0.5, 1, 1.5 or 2 seconds, 1.5 by default, and starts and lands gently.

The button, the band at the top of the screen and its edge turn green while it is on, and the button now and then shows the current amount, such as −50%. It multiplies with the grand master. Locked fixtures are left alone. A fader set as a switch is not dimmed, but if its fixture is marked it goes OFF while BATTERY SAVE is on. With nothing marked it is dim and does not turn on; hold it to reach its settings. While it is on, a dimmed fixture's fader fills only as high as the light really is, and the part held back shows as a shadow with a green ↓. The ↓ fades in once the light has finished dropping, and goes at once when it starts to return. To bring one fixture back for now, turn on Skip BATTERY SAVE at the top of its panel; it stays back until BATTERY SAVE is turned off.

This dims your lights. It is not an iPhone battery setting.

HISTORY

Tap or hold HISTORY on Home to see the states you have been through. Choose a row to go back to it. HERE marks where you are.

  • It keeps the last 50. Going back and then working leaves the old states in place and adds the new one at the end.
  • It covers intensity, color, output on and off, limits, raw values, effects, GM, B.O., the patch and the order of the faders.
  • Stepping back past a patch change keeps the list, and you can step forward again. A deleted fixture comes back with its place in Scenes and looks.
  • Each patch edit, and each press of B.O. or a GM key, is a step of its own. Skip BATTERY SAVE and anything done in BLIND are not in it.
  • Fixture Lock is outside it. A locked fixture does not move when you step back.
  • Scene recalls are recorded. Stepping back or forward across one also puts back which Scene is current, so AUTO UPDATE does not record into the wrong one. Overwriting a Scene's contents cannot be undone.
  • You cannot pull out one change on its own. You go back to the whole state at that moment.
  • It is kept with each show on this device. Quitting and reopening Kanau, or opening the show again, brings it back.

The fade on a recall is set by Recall Fade Time. HISTORY is unavailable with nothing to go back to.

ZEN

Tap ZEN in a fixture's panel for a black screen with one large fader and its value. It is there for fixtures whose intensity you can set. It opens on a selection as well — hold a round icon, or open COLOR, or hold a model or group button. The name at the bottom says what you have: 3 fixtures, or KEY · 8 fixtures.

With more than one, it follows the rules the Intensity row in the color panel already follows. The number on screen is the first fixture's. Opening changes nothing. The first time you drag, the rest land where the first one lands — they do not keep the spread they had — and each stops inside its own limits. If the first one cannot move, none of them move.

Drag anywhere on the screen to work it, relative as usual. FINE, under TILT at the top left, is the same FINE as on Home: tap it for FINE, FINE+ and off, or hold it for as long as you need it. On a single fixture the settings at the top right hold the limits, TILT's angle and FIXTURE SETTINGS, which opens the fixture's panel and comes back to ZEN when you close it; with more than one they are not there. A fixture set as Switch shows a rocker instead of a fader: each press turns it ON at its upper limit or OFF at its lower. The way out is the ✕ at the top left: tapping the screen does not leave, and neither does moving the fader and letting go.

TILT at the top left hands the fader to the angle of the phone. Flat is the bottom of its travel and straight up is the top — 0 and 100 with no limits set, and the limits themselves where you have set them. It keeps working after you take your hand away, and it follows a quick hand without lagging behind. It does not grab at once: it waits until the tilt meets the level the fader is already on, so nothing jumps. The settings choose which angle counts as the top — 90°, 60° or 45°. A smaller angle reaches the top with less movement. Reaching the top gives one short vibration; holding it there does not repeat it. Pulling the fader with a finger turns it off, and so does leaving ZEN.

+ FADER at the top right adds another fader: up to three on iPhone and five on iPad, counting the first. It opens a list of Groups and Fixtures; tap one to add it as a fader of its own and close the list. A fixture already on another fader is dimmed. The screen divides into columns, each worked on its own, relative as usual, with its number at the top and its name at the bottom. A group reads like KEY · 8 fixtures and follows the rule above. Each column has its own ⚙ at the bottom, with its limits, FIXTURE SETTINGS and, from the second column on, Remove fader. With two or more faders the ⚙ at the top right is gone, and TILT switches off and is not shown; FINE takes its place. Back to one fader, both return, with TILT off.

11 Saving and sharing shows

A show holds one job: the patch, the groups, the order of the faders, the Scenes and the current look, with its Fixture Locks.

There is nothing to press. Changes are saved as you make them.

When it saves

WhatWhen
Patch, groups, order of the faders, ScenesAs you change them
The current look and fixture settingsAbout two seconds after you stop, and when the app goes to the background

Next launch restores the last show as it was saved, and the Scene you had recalled, unless that Scene has been deleted or you quit in BLIND. Output is not restored: Kanau opens with output off (chapter 02). Under MANUAL UPDATE, changes you had not recorded yet still light UPDATE after reopening. The very last change before a quit is not guaranteed, so use Export Show File when you need a file to keep or to hand on. The shows folder can be seen in the Files app.

Settings → Shows

ItemWhat it does
Current ShowRenames the show you are in
VersionsEarlier states of the current show. Restore goes back to one; the show as it is now is kept as a version first
Save AsStores the current state as another show and carries on in the copy
Export Show FileSaves first, then asks what to take. All is the whole show; Patch and Groups takes the fixtures, their numbers, addresses and names, the fader order and the groups, without Scenes or the current look; Patch Only leaves out the groups as well. Output, MIDI and Session settings stay on this device. Then choose where from the share sheet
Import Show FileBrings a .kanau in as a new show. Your current show is untouched, and this device keeps its own Output, MIDI and Session settings
New ShowName it and Create. You get an empty show, and Patch opens
Other ShowsOpens a stored show. ⧉ duplicates. ✕ moves it to Discarded, after a confirmation titled with its name

The show you are in is named in amber beside Shows and carries a check under Current Show. Starting a new show, or opening another, asks first — Keep Show 1?, with what is in it, and Keep, Discard or Cancel. It does not ask whether to save: saving has already happened, so the question is whether to keep. Discard is red but it does not delete — the show moves to Discarded, where Restore brings it back. To remove one for good, use its ✕ there and confirm. A show with no fixtures and no Scenes is tidied away without asking. When you open another show, the question also says that Kanau's output switches to that show.

Versions are kept on this device: about one an hour while the show changes, plus one before each restore; after 10, the oldest goes. Versions appears under Current Show once there is one. A name that starts with ".", ends in ".history" or "-cues", or contains "/" or ":" cannot be used for a show, and names that differ only in capital letters count as the same name.

A .kanau that arrives by Files or AirDrop can be opened with Kanau and comes in as a new show; while BLIND is on, it is refused with a vibration. A .kanaumidi is treated as a MIDI mapping file.

Opening and recovery

With nothing stored, the demo show opens. An older show that has no stored look opens with the intensity down.

If the file cannot be read you get Saved patch could not be read. Showing an empty rig; the file is left as it is., and it starts empty. The original file is kept and not overwritten.

A failed save shows Patch was not saved. in red. Chapter 14 covers what to do.

What is not in the show

WhatWhere it lives
SAVED effect settingsOn the device, available to every show
Custom FixturesOn the device. The definitions of patched fixtures are kept in the show as well
Stored ★ colors and temperaturesOn the device. Colors per model and mode, temperatures shared
MIDI mappingOn the device. Exportable on its own as .kanaumidi
Output, Session, display settings, languageOn the device. Whether output is sending is not kept: it is off at every launch
HISTORYOn the device, one for each show
VersionsOn the device, beside each show. Not shown in the Files app
Piano ＋ / Piano −, Strap LockOn the device

Settings → Settings

Language (System or one of 15 languages), the various fade times, the BATTERY SAVE amount, Piano ＋ and Piano −, Strap Lock, which number to show, the All row in Patch, and whether gels appear. A new language applies after you quit and reopen Kanau. Text size follows the iOS setting.

12 MIDI controllers (Advanced)

Mapping the knobs and buttons of a MIDI controller onto fixtures and controls.

This chapter covers the Learn-style screen.

Connecting and mapping

  1. Turn on MIDI Controller in Settings → MIDI. It is off by default.
  2. Check that your gear appears under Inputs (None when there is none) and that Last CC changes as you move something.
  3. Start with MIDI Channel on OMNI, then narrow it to 1–16 if you need to.
  4. Map with Learn under Faders & Switches or Buttons.
  5. Turn a knob while Turn… is showing. For a button, press it while Press… is showing. Closing Settings first cancels Learn, and nothing is mapped.

The gear this was built against is the Behringer X-Touch Mini and Compact, in Standard mode sending absolute values. MC mode is not used.

What a knob follows

A knob follows a position on screen, not a fixture. Change page or group and its target changes with it. Faders & Switches lists the positions in order: ten on an iPhone, and on an iPad one for each fader on screen, up to 40. Each Fader N takes a knob, and the Switch N row indented under it takes a button. GRAND MASTER comes after Fader 10, then Buttons. A knob on a fader set as a switch switches it as it passes the middle.

A mapping set up per fixture in an earlier version opens as screen positions.

When a knob does nothing at first

If the knob and the value on screen disagree, nothing moves until the knob passes the value on screen. That is deliberate: it stops the level jumping. The same applies after you change page or group, and after you unlock a fixture; while a fixture is locked, its knob does not take it. On a guest in a session, knobs take nothing while the link is amber or red or the host is refusing its changes; once that clears, pass the value again. If something else moves the value a knob has taken — GO, a finger on screen, a Scene button or the GM chip — the knob lets go until it passes the value again.

With MIDI Controller on, turn on Send Values Back and Kanau sends each knob's current level back to the controller. Empty positions come back as 0.

Buttons, and the mapping file

Under Buttons you can map FINE, PIANO, Page ‹, Page ›, BACK, NEXT, BATTERY SAVE and each Scene. BACK and NEXT do what they do in Scenes, and BATTERY SAVE what its button at the top does. Scenes folds away; its heading keeps the count, with · N learned once any Scene has a Note. Deleting a Scene removes its Note. Switch N presses the ⏻ under Fader N and does what that fixture's Power Switch says. While BLIND is on, MIDI follows the screen, except GRAND MASTER, which still acts on the lights. B.O. cannot be mapped. One button carries one action. Fixture Lock applies to MIDI as well.

Export and Import under MIDI Map File write and read the mapping as a .kanaumidi file, separate from the show. A file that breaks the rules is refused with This file could not be read., and the current mapping stays.

13 Working from several devices — Session

iPhones and iPads on one show. Only the host sends DMX; the others work the same console through it.

A session lets devices on the same network drive one show. A guest sends what you do to the host. If the host stops, nothing takes over automatically. Every device in a session must run the same version of Kanau.

Who holds what

HostGuest
Sending DMXYesNo
Owns the showYesBorrows it
Changing the patchYesNo
Where a Scene is savedThe host's showSent to the host
Working the lightYesOnce the host taps Allow

When both touch the same fixture, the host wins. The guest sees TAKEN.

Starting a session

  1. On the device that will send, choose Settings → Settings → Session → Host. A QR code appears. Until the device is on Wi-Fi or a wired network, the section says The code appears here when this device is on Wi-Fi or a wired network., and the code appears by itself once it is.
  2. On the other device, choose Settings → Settings → Session → Join, then Scan Code.
  3. Point the camera at the host's QR code. The first time, Kanau asks to use the camera.
  4. Check for Joined and the connection state.

There is no number to type: the QR code is the only way in. With camera access turned off, the screen says Camera access is off. Allow it in Settings to join. A QR code that is not Kanau's gives This is not a Kanau session code. Looking for the host… means the guest has not reached the host yet.

A guest starts out watching. Until the host taps Allow, the status line reads WATCH ONLY, the Session section says Waiting for the host to allow control., and nothing the guest touches reaches the light. Up to 8 guests can control at once.

The host's list

With Hosting on, the host's Session section shows the QR code, New Devices, New Code, and Devices: one row for each guest, with its name and Pending, Can control or Watching. The heading counts how many can control, such as 2 of 8 can control.

ControlWhat it does
AllowLets that guest work the light. A guest that has just joined is Pending, and only watches
Take BackReturns it to Watching. What it was holding is let go
RemoveDrops it. It cannot join again until you tap New Code, and it sees The host removed this device.
New DevicesTurned off, no new guest can join, and one that tries sees The host is not accepting new devices. Guests already in stay
New CodeAsks first, then drops every guest and makes a new QR code. A guest with the old code sees The host's code has changed. Scan the new code.

Once 8 guests can control, Allow is not offered.

What a guest can do

This is for a guest the host has allowed; a guest that is watching can do none of it.

The guest canThe host doesEach device keeps its own
Faders, color and gels, on fixtures and cellsAdding, removing and changing the patch, names, labels, SwitchWhich group and page is showing, which tab
Recalling Scenes, SAVE to store, UPDATE into the recalled Scene, and AUTO UPDATE / MANUAL UPDATE, which is shared with the hostReordering Scenes, deleting, renaming, fade, lock; HISTORY; BLINDFINE, 10 / 5, PIXELS, PIANO mode
⏻, GM, B.O., BATTERY SAVE with its depth and Skip BATTERY SAVEOutput, Shows, DMX MonitorDisplay settings, language, gels, Strap Lock
Limits, Fixture Lock, clearing a selection, reordering the fadersFade times, Piano ＋ / Piano −, Power SwitchMIDI mapping, stored ★ colors

The PIXELS and FIXTURES sections of the COLOR panel (chapter 05) appear on the host only. A Scene stored from the guest is written by the host, and the host refuses SAVE with Not accepted while a fade is running. The guest's own show file is untouched, and Leave Session puts it back. While you are a guest, opening or importing a show is refused with a vibration.

Effects and the guest

Every effect action reaches the host.

ActionFrom the guest
Applying an effectWorks
PAUSE and RESUMEWorks
RELEASE, on the fixtures you selectedWorks
RELEASE ALLWorks
EDIT, RELEASE, START, PAUSE, RESUME and CLEAR on a row of the Effects tabWorks
Clearing a cell's effectsWorks
SIGNAL: BACK, NEXT, PLAY, PAUSE, REPEAT, NEXT STOPS AT, ADVANCED, and filling the signalsWorks
START ALLWorks

Working at the same time, and losing the link

What the guest changes appears on the guest's screen at once. If the host touches the same fixture, the host wins and the guest sees TAKEN. A fixture the other device is working shows a cyan edge with a name.

ConnectionState
GreenConnected to the host
AmberNothing from the host for about 3 seconds
RedNothing for about 15 seconds. The host is no longer available. appears

If the link drops, the guest keeps showing the last state. It does not leave on its own, so use Leave Session. After reconnecting, faders are still relative.

No internet is needed. The devices must be able to reach each other on the same network. Client isolation, a firewall and similar settings can block the session even where DMX gets through.

14 Troubleshooting

Arranged by what you are seeing. Work down the list.

Nothing lights up

What you seeWhat to do
OUTPUT OFFNothing has been sent since Kanau opened. Tap it and slide (chapter 02)
IdleCheck that a network is enabled in Settings → Output
BlockedTap it to open Settings → Output, which prints a red line that names what stopped it and what to do. Follow that line
Blocked U1, with a universe numberAnother sender is already on that universe. Tap it for Join, Send … Only or Cancel
No nodeTap it to open Settings → Output. Check the node's power, network, address and protocol settings
B.O.Tap it to clear the blackout
GM 0Open GM and use →100
U1 OFFTurn the universe back on in Output → Universes
A purple ⏻ or fixture iconTurn the fixture's output back on
A green BATTERY SAVE, or a shadow with a green ↓ on a faderClear it, or turn on Skip BATTERY SAVE for that fixture
A low Upper LimitCheck the fixture's limits
⚠ in PatchFix the overlapping address or the run past 512
A mode that does not matchSet the same DMX mode as the fixture itself
An amber BLIND at the top leftYou are in BLIND, and what you do does not reach the lights. Tap it to leave

No node is found

If Network shows No reply, check that the iPhone and the node are on the same network. If AUTO does not reach it, use UNICAST and enter the node's address. Run RESCAN after changing anything about the connection.

Check the node's own Art-Net and sACN switches, its address and its universe. As an example, the LumenRadio CRMX Stardust ships with Art-Net and sACN turned off.

If you are joining a Stardust's or an Aputure Sidus Four's own Wi-Fi, check which band the gear supports. On an external access point, 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz clients can often reach each other; a different band does not always mean a different network.

On a Stardust, lower case on the output display means no data is arriving and upper case means it is. Check the manufacturer's own manual for anything model-specific. Gear that does not answer polling shows 0 under Nodes Answering even while receiving.

It flickers

Check that the same fixture is not being fed from both the network and Bluetooth, or from more than one console or DMX source. Look at any SHARED or Blocked message and cut the paths down to one. The same universe number on two paths is not by itself evidence that they meet (chapter 02).

Another control app, or a setting on the fixture, can also cause it.

It stutters, or reacts slowly

Open Settings → Output and read it from the top. If it stops at one of these, you do not need to look further down.

Network Output   is the console sending at all
   ↓
Clock            is it jammed inside the phone
   ↓
Touch → DMX     is the trip from finger to packet slow
   ↓
Node RTT         is the network or the gear slow
   ↓
Fixture          is the light itself slow
What you seeWhat to look at
Network Output is NothingDestination, network, iOS permissions
Clock over 100 msThe phone. Close panels, restart the app if you need to
Nodes answer, but a light does not respondThe address AUTO is sending to. If the node reports itself wrongly, try BROADCAST
Clock is fine but the round trip is longWi-Fi congestion, the access point, the gear, the path
The numbers are fine but the light lagsSmoothing on the fixture, its input path, another app driving it

BROADCAST helps when AUTO's destination is the problem. For other causes it will not help, and may add load.

Some faders do nothing

Check the fixture's limits, its Lock, and whether its output is on. A fader that shows ON and OFF is set as a switch; turn off Switch in its panel to get the fader back. The fader curve in Kanau is linear; a dimmer curve in the fixture can make the bottom half feel flat. Check the fixture itself, or Dim curve under Channels.

On a fixture imported from GDTF, wrong intensity or color usually means the roles are wrong. Fix them in Channel Roles. To carry the fix into fixtures you patch later, edit the definition under Custom Fixtures.

A button does nothing

What you seeWhy, and what to do
A purple wash over the screenSCREEN LOCK. Drag the slider in the middle to the right
A green 🔒Clear the Fixture Lock
COLOR or EFFECT is greySelect a fixture. COLOR also needs the fixture to have color
EFFECT reads N RUNNINGNothing is selected. Select fixtures, or use the Effects tab
PIXELS is greyThere is no pixel fixture on the page
HISTORY is inactiveThere is nothing to go back to
The number buttons do not change intensityPiano mode is on LOCK. Use ＋ −
Home under Channels is inactiveIt is already at the default
Home for Pan or Tilt does nothingIt needs a hold, not a tap
A Scene will not updateCheck MANUAL UPDATE, and Lock This Scene
A guest cannot edit the patchDo it on the host
A guest cannot change anything, and the status line reads WATCH ONLYThe host taps Allow in Settings → Settings → Session

The color is wrong

What you seeWhat to check
A different color from the one you setWhether the Patch mode matches the fixture's own DMX mode
No color controls at allWhether the fixture has color. Mixed models show only the shared items (chapter 05)
The color temperature stops shortYou are at the edge of the fixture's range. It reads MIN or MAX
An imported fixture is offCheck Channel Roles (chapter 06)
White pulls green or magentaGreen / Magenta may not be at 0. Back to neutral resets it

A fixture does not behave

Check first that the Patch mode matches the fixture's own. When that is wrong, intensity arrives as color and color arrives as position.

A definition imported from GDTF can have roles assigned differently from the real fixture. Correct them in Channel Roles (chapter 06). To carry it into future patches, edit the Custom Fixtures definition.

Check anything marked Imported data is not verified. against the real fixture.

A Scene keeps changing on its own

AUTO UPDATE is on to begin with, so anything you do after recalling a Scene is recorded back into it (chapter 08).

Switch the top of Scenes to MANUAL UPDATE and nothing goes in until you tap UPDATE. For Scenes you want left alone whatever the mode, turn on Lock This Scene under that Scene's Settings. You can still recall them and still work the light; nothing is recorded.

A Scene will not record

What to check
MANUAL UPDATENothing goes in until you tap UPDATE under that row
Lock This SceneNothing is recorded while it is on, in either mode
You are on a guestReordering, deleting and renaming are the host's (chapter 13)
What is never storedBATTERY SAVE, Power Switch, limits and Fixture Lock. Everything else comes back, GM and B.O. included (chapter 08)

The session will not connect

If Looking for the host… will not clear, check these.

  • Both devices are on the same network. No internet is needed
  • You scanned the host's current QR code. New Code makes older codes useless, and the guest then says The host's code has changed. Scan the new code.
  • Camera access for Kanau is on in iOS Settings
  • The host shows its QR code. Until it is on Wi-Fi or a wired network it shows a line saying so instead
  • Client isolation or a firewall is not blocking device-to-device traffic
  • Every device runs the same version of Kanau

DMX can get through on a network where device-to-device traffic is blocked.

Something stays lit on blackout

Check Fixture Lock. The green 🔒 n at the top counts what is still lit. Clear the lock on those fixtures. A lock whose fixture was deleted also stays lit; press UNLOCK on its row in DMX Monitor.

The app quit, or the link dropped

Restarting restores the last saved show and look, and the Scene you had recalled, with output off: slide to send again. The very last changes before a quit may not be there.

What your lights do after the app or the link stops depends on the node's and the fixture's own hold-last-look settings. Check the gear if you need them to hold.

A save failed

Patch was not saved. means the save failed. Check the free space on the device, and if you can, write the current state out with Export Show File. Make sure the export finished before carrying on. Dismissing the warning with × does not mean it saved.

If a file cannot be read, open another show from Other Shows, Import a .kanau you exported earlier, or restore an earlier state under Versions. The file that could not be read is kept.

Checking the DMX values

Settings → DMX Monitor shows all 512 channels of each universe. It only shows them; the one thing you can do there is UNLOCK a lock whose fixture was deleted.
